# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/service.py
================================================================================
"""Companion servers an integration provides, run as containers while something uses them."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal, Protocol, TypedDict

from pydantic import BaseModel

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint, PeripheralChange
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.need import Need
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.peripheral import NoSettings, Peripheral

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.platform import Platform


class Healthcheck(TypedDict, total=False):
    test: list[str]
    interval: str
    timeout: str
    start_period: str
    retries: int


class ComposeService(TypedDict, total=False):
    """A Docker Compose service definition, the keys services use typed (a typo fails type checking, not the start);
    another key goes here first. Its strings are templates: see `Service`."""

    image: str
    build: str
    command: list[str]
    entrypoint: list[str]
    environment: dict[str, str]
    volumes: list[str]
    devices: list[str]
    tmpfs: list[str]
    network_mode: Literal["host", "bridge", "none"]
    userns_mode: Literal["host"]
    user: str
    privileged: bool
    hostname: str
    cap_add: list[str]
    cap_drop: list[str]
    group_add: list[str]
    healthcheck: Healthcheck


class ServiceHost(Protocol):
    """What runs a `Service`'s container, bound to its ``container`` need: the runtime's `Compose`."""

    def provided(self, service: Service) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        """Its ``provides`` rendered: the host ports it got, the params it renders."""
        ...

    async def up(self, service: Service):
        """Run its container; return once it serves."""
        ...

    async def down(self, service: Service): ...

    def is_current(self, service: Service) -> bool:
        """Whether its container still runs what it would render now."""
        ...


CONTAINER_HOST = Need[ServiceHost]("container", ["compose"])  # what every service needs


class Service[S: BaseModel = Any](Peripheral[S]):
    """A companion server an integration provides, such as Matter's matterjs-server: a container that runs only while
    something that runs is bound to one of its endpoints. The integration lists it next to its controller, which
    `Need`s what it provides.

    ``compose`` is its Docker Compose service definition (image, environment, volumes, …); its strings may hold
    ``{data}`` (its own documents folder), ``{peripherals.<family>.url}``, ``{settings.<field>}``,
    ``{platform.<fact>}`` (``{platform.region}``), ``{host.interface|uid|gid|listen_address}`` and ``{ports.<name>}``.
    A format spec turns a value into text: ``{x:!text}`` renders ``text`` when ``x`` is empty, ``{x:?text}`` when it
    isn't; a list item that renders empty is left out, so
    ``"volumes": ["{peripherals.ble.url:?/run/dbus:/run/dbus:ro}"]`` mounts D-Bus only while an adapter is bound. One
    on the host network (``network_mode: host``) listens on ``{host.listen_address}``: loopback unless the host opens
    its services to the LAN for a lab harness.
    The ``params`` of the ``provides`` endpoints render the same way, which is how a consumer learns what its service
    got: ``params={"adapter": "{peripherals.ble.url}"}``. ``settings`` is the model of its options, its ``Settings``.

    ``ports`` names the host ports it listens on, each with the port it *prefers*, not a fixed one: the runtime uses it
    when free, else assigns another (45800-45999), keeps the choice across restarts, and fills ``{ports.<name>}`` in
    ``compose`` and in the ``provides`` URLs. Integrations never read a port: they connect through
    ``self.peripherals.endpoint(<family>).url``.

    Its start returns once its container runs, its ports answer, `provision` finished and `is_healthy` says so. A
    change of what its needs are bound to or of the platform's facts recreates it only when it renders otherwise.
    Subclass it to hook in: `provision` sets up what it runs, `is_healthy` checks more; a ``start`` of your own may tell
    what it learned once it serves (``self.output.peripheral_did_learn``).
    """

    is_on_demand = True
    start_timeout: float = 30 * 60  # its first start pulls its image

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        compose: ComposeService,
        needs: Sequence[Need] = (),
        provides: Sequence[Endpoint] = (),
        settings: type[S] = NoSettings,  # ty: ignore[invalid-parameter-default]  (none: it takes none)
        ports: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,  # name -> PREFERRED host port; see the docstring
    ):
        self.name, self.compose, self.needs, self.templates = name, compose, [*needs, CONTAINER_HOST], provides
        self.settings_model, self.ports = settings, ports or {}

    @property
    def Settings(self) -> type[S]:
        return self.settings_model

    @property
    def host(self) -> ServiceHost | None:
        """The container host its need is bound to."""
        return self.peripherals.instance(CONTAINER_HOST)

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return self.host.provided(self) if self.host else self.templates

    async def start(self):
        if not self.host:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"Nothing runs containers here: run {self.name} yourself and pin what it provides"
            )
        await self.host.up(self)

    async def stop(self):
        if self.host:
            await self.host.down(self)

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        """Its container is recreated only when it would render otherwise now, or on another container host."""
        return change.family != CONTAINER_HOST.family and self.host is not None and self.host.is_current(self)

    async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Platform) -> bool:
        """Its container is recreated only when it would render otherwise now."""
        return self.host.is_current(self) if self.host else True

    async def provision(self, endpoint: Endpoint):
        """Set up one of its endpoints once it answers, e.g. form a network. Called each time its container is
        (re)created, cancelled when it stops: keep it idempotent."""
        return

    async def is_healthy(self) -> bool:
        """A check of its own on top of its ports answering; asked until it says yes."""
        return True

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"{type(self).__name__}({self.name!r})"

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/peripherals/usb.py
================================================================================
"""Drivers that recognise USB devices for the runtime's USB scanner."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, ClassVar

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.endpoint import Endpoint
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals.peripheral import Peripheral

USB_DRIVER = "usb-driver"  # the family a driver provides itself as, to the scanners that need every driver


class UsbDriver(Peripheral):
    """One kind of USB device: recognises which firmware a device runs and says what each firmware serves.

    The scanner asks its own drivers first, then the ones integrations provide next to their controller: Zigbee's
    tells the radios only zigpy knows apart. ``firmwares`` maps a firmware to what it serves: ``{device}`` in a URL is
    the device's path, ``params`` its serial settings (soldered hardware may wire them differently).
    """

    is_on_demand = True  # only while a scanner uses it
    firmwares: ClassVar[Mapping[str, Sequence[Endpoint]]] = {}
    bluetooth: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset()  # firmwares that serve Bluetooth too (multiprotocol over CPC)

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return [Endpoint(USB_DRIVER, self.name, self.name, is_shared=True, instance=self)]

    async def identify(self, path: str) -> str | tuple[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None:
        """The firmware the device at ``path`` runs, or None when it isn't one of its kind; with the serial settings it
        found the device at where they may differ from the firmware's, ``("deconz", {"baud": 38400})``: the device's
        endpoints take them."""
        return None

    def serves(self, firmware: str | None, path: str, params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> list[Endpoint]:
        """What ``firmware`` serves on the device at ``path``, ``params`` overriding its serial settings."""
        endpoints = self.firmwares.get(firmware or "", [])
        return [replace(e, url=e.url.format(device=path), params={**e.params, **(params or {})}) for e in endpoints]

    def flashable(self, path: str, channel: str) -> list[str]:
        """Firmwares the device at ``path`` can be switched to on the ``stable`` or ``dev`` channel."""
        return []

    async def flash(self, path: str, firmware: str, channel: str, cache: Path):
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{type(self).__name__} can't flash")

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/platform.py
================================================================================
"""The host every peripheral runs on, as its ``self.platform``: the facts it knows and its resources."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository.memory import DeviceRepositoryMemory
from majordom_integration_sdk.repository.protocol import DeviceRepositoryProtocol
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.credentials import WifiCredentials

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral

type MakeDeviceRepository = Callable[[str], AbstractAsyncContextManager[DeviceRepositoryProtocol]]


def _in_memory() -> MakeDeviceRepository:
    store: dict[UUID, dict[str, Any]] = {}  # shared by the repositories of every peripheral
    return lambda key: DeviceRepositoryMemory(key, store).session()


@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Platform:
    """The host every peripheral runs on, the same object for all of them as ``self.platform``: a controller is given
    it, ``peripherals(platform)``, and the runtime sets it on the others. It holds the facts the host knows as plain
    fields, and its resources, scoped to the peripheral passed::

        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repository:
            ...
        cache = self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "cache.json"

    Facts change only by replacement: the host builds a new platform (``dataclasses.replace``) and gives it to the
    runtime (`Runtime.update_platform`), which points every peripheral at it and tells the ones that run
    (``platform_facts_did_change``). Read ``self.platform`` when you need a fact: a platform kept holds the old ones.
    """

    # Where each peripheral gets a folder of its own, by its key: the Hub's, or a local one under the dev runner
    documents_root: Path
    # One unit of work on the device repository, scoped to the devices of the peripheral keyed; in memory by default
    make_device_repository: MakeDeviceRepository = field(default_factory=_in_memory)
    region: str | None = None  # RF region for sub-GHz radios, a Z-Wave JS name: "Europe", "USA", …
    wifi: WifiCredentials | None = None  # the network to provision Wi-Fi devices onto
    thread_dataset: str | None = None  # active operational dataset of the hub's Thread network, hex TLVs

    def documents_folder(self, peripheral: Peripheral) -> Path:
        """The folder of ``peripheral``, by its key, created on use: what it keeps across restarts that doesn't belong
        in the device database (certificates, protocol caches, a container's data)."""
        folder = self.documents_root / peripheral.key
        folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return folder

    def device_repository(self, peripheral: Peripheral) -> AbstractAsyncContextManager[DeviceRepositoryProtocol]:
        """One unit of work on the device repository, scoped to the devices of ``peripheral``, by its key: a
        controller's is its slug, the ``integration`` of every `Device` it keeps."""
        return self.make_device_repository(peripheral.key)

================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/_record.py
================================================================================
"""Internal record helpers shared by the SDK's repository implementations.

A stored record is one JSON-safe dict per device holding *everything* known about it —
info, ``integration_data`` and ``parameters`` (from a :class:`DeviceState`). A ``Device``
lacks the parameters, and a ``DeviceState`` built without ``integration_data`` doesn't hold
the stored one; merging keeps both halves and lets a read deserialize into whichever view
(``as_``) the caller asks for.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState

type Record = dict[str, Any]


def dump(device: BaseModel, exclude: set[str] | None = None) -> Record:
    """JSON-safe dump, so records round-trip identically through memory or SQLite.

    Goes through ``model_dump_json`` rather than ``model_dump(mode="json")`` — the JSON
    serializer is the one these models are actually exercised against (``ParameterState``
    base64-encodes its ``bytes`` value there), so it's what the SQLite rows already store.
    """
    return json.loads(device.model_dump_json(exclude=exclude))


def merge(base: Record | None, device: Device | DeviceState) -> Record:
    """Merge a device into an existing record without clobbering the other view's fields: an unset
    ``integration_data`` (its default) only where the record has none (the ``{}`` or null the Hub stores a device with
    before pairing is none), so that filling the default in place counts."""
    unset = {"integration_data"} - device.model_fields_set if base and base.get("integration_data") else set()
    return {**(base or {}), **dump(device, exclude=unset)}


__all__ = ["Record", "dump", "merge"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/memory.py
================================================================================
"""In-memory :class:`DeviceRepositoryProtocol` implementation.

A legitimate, lightweight persistence choice for standalone/dev runs and tests — not a
mock. State lives in a dict for the process lifetime; use :class:`SqliteDeviceRepository`
when you need it to survive a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository._record import Record, dump, merge
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState, ParameterVisibility


class DeviceRepositoryMemory:
    """Stores device records in a dict shared across sessions.

    Pass ``integration`` to scope every operation to that integration's devices (the guard
    the Hub sets when handing a repository to a controller). ``None`` gives full access.
    """

    def __init__(self, integration: str | None = None, store: dict[UUID, Record] | None = None):
        self.integration = integration
        self._store: dict[UUID, Record] = store if store is not None else {}

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def session(self) -> AsyncGenerator[DeviceRepositoryMemory]:
        """One unit of work: what ``Platform.make_device_repository`` returns for its integration."""
        yield self

    def _in_scope(self, record: Record) -> bool:
        return self.integration is None or record.get("integration") == self.integration

    def _owned(self, device_id: UUID) -> Record | None:
        record = self._store.get(device_id)
        return record if record is not None and self._in_scope(record) else None

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        return [as_.model_validate(r) for r in self._store.values() if self._in_scope(r)]

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        if not record:
            return None
        return next(
            (ParameterState.model_validate(p) for p in record.get("parameters", []) if p["id"] == str(parameter_id)),
            None,
        )

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        if self.integration is not None and device.integration != self.integration:
            raise PermissionError(f"Device {device.id} is outside integration scope {self.integration!r}")
        base = self._store.pop(previous_id, None) if previous_id is not None and previous_id != device.id else None
        self._store[device.id] = merge(base if base is not None else self._store.get(device.id), device)

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        record = self._owned(device_id)
        if not record:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown or out-of-scope device {device_id}")
        updated = dump(parameter_state)
        record["parameters"] = [
            updated if p["id"] == str(parameter_state.id) else p for p in record.get("parameters", [])
        ]

    # Hub-internal (not on DeviceRepositoryProtocol); still scope-checked.

    async def update_parameter_visibility(self, parameter_id: UUID, visibility: ParameterVisibility):
        for record in self._store.values():
            if not self._in_scope(record):
                continue
            for parameter in record.get("parameters", []):
                if parameter["id"] == str(parameter_id):
                    parameter["visibility"] = visibility.value
                    return

    async def delete(self, device_id: UUID):
        if self._owned(device_id):
            self._store.pop(device_id, None)


__all__ = ["DeviceRepositoryMemory"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/protocol.py
================================================================================
"""The device-repository interface a controller talks to.

A controller never touches a database directly — it goes through this protocol, obtained
from its platform's ``device_repository(self)`` (an async context manager scoping one unit of
work). The
Hub backs it with its shared SQLAlchemy database; the SDK ships two first-class
implementations for standalone/dev use — :class:`DeviceRepositoryMemory` and
:class:`SqliteDeviceRepository`.

**Integration scope.** The repository is bound to one integration at construction, so there
is no ``integration`` argument on the reads: an integration only ever sees its own devices.
Out-of-scope reads come back ``None``/empty and out-of-scope writes raise — a guard against
carelessness, not a security boundary. Constructing with ``integration=None`` gives full
access (the Hub's own higher-level use).

**Typed reads.** ``as_`` deserializes into your own ``Device[MyData]`` /
``DeviceState[MyData, MyParameterData]`` (or a subclass), so ``integration_data`` comes back
typed instead of a bare dict::

    async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
        device = await repo.get(device_id, as_=MyDevice)  # class MyDevice(Device[MyData])

**Not here on purpose:** ``delete`` and ``update_parameter_visibility`` are Hub-internal
lifecycle operations. They exist on the concrete implementations, but are kept off this
protocol so an integration can't reach past its scope.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState


@runtime_checkable
class DeviceRepositoryProtocol(Protocol):
    """Persistence for one integration's paired devices and their parameter states."""

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        """Every paired device in scope, deserialized as ``as_``."""
        ...

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        """The device (info + ``integration_data``) as ``as_``, or ``None`` if unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        """The device with its parameter states as ``as_``, or ``None`` if unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        """One parameter's current state, or ``None`` if the device/parameter is unknown/out of scope."""
        ...

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        """Insert or update a device, merging into whatever is already stored.

        Saving a ``Device`` updates its info/``integration_data``; saving a ``DeviceState``
        updates its info/``parameters``, and its ``integration_data`` only when it was given
        one — neither clobbers the other's fields. ``previous_id``
        renames an existing record before the write (pairing turning a provisional discovery
        id into the device's final id), carrying its stored data over. Rejects a device
        outside the bound integration's scope.
        """
        ...

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        """Update a single parameter's value/state on an existing in-scope device."""
        ...


__all__ = ["DeviceRepositoryProtocol"]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/repository/sqlite.py
================================================================================
"""File-backed :class:`DeviceRepositoryProtocol` on the standard-library ``sqlite3``.

No third-party dependency: each device is stored as one row of JSON (the record already
stores pythonic parameter values as JSON via Pydantic). Suitable
for a standalone integration that needs its paired devices to survive a restart; the Hub
uses its own SQLAlchemy-backed repository instead.

``sqlite3`` is synchronous; calls are cheap and local, so the async methods invoke it
directly. Obtain a session with :meth:`session` (opens a connection, commits on clean exit).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.repository._record import Record, dump, merge
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Device, DeviceState
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterState, ParameterVisibility


class SqliteDeviceRepository:
    """Persists device records as JSON rows in a SQLite file.

    Pass ``integration`` to scope every operation to that integration's devices (the guard
    the Hub sets when handing a repository to a controller). ``None`` gives full access.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path, integration: str | None = None):
        self.path = str(path)
        self.integration = integration
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices ("
                "  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, uuid TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,"
                "  integration TEXT NOT NULL, data TEXT NOT NULL)"
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        return conn

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def session(self) -> AsyncGenerator[SqliteDeviceRepository]:
        """One unit of work: what ``Platform.make_device_repository`` returns for its integration."""
        # A fresh connection per unit of work; sharing one across concurrent tasks is unsafe.
        self._conn = self._connect()
        try:
            yield self
            self._conn.commit()
        finally:
            self._conn.close()
            del self._conn

    def _cursor(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        conn = getattr(self, "_conn", None)
        if conn is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Use `async with repo.session():` before calling repository methods")
        return conn

    def _record(self, device_id: UUID) -> Record | None:
        """The stored record for an in-scope device, or None."""
        if self.integration is None:
            row = self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(device_id),)).fetchone()
        else:
            row = (
                self._cursor()
                .execute(
                    "SELECT data FROM devices WHERE uuid = ? AND integration = ?",
                    (str(device_id), self.integration),
                )
                .fetchone()
            )
        return json.loads(row["data"]) if row else None

    def _write(self, record: Record):
        self._cursor().execute(
            "INSERT INTO devices (uuid, integration, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT(uuid) DO UPDATE SET integration = excluded.integration, data = excluded.data",
            (record["id"], record["integration"], json.dumps(record)),
        )

    async def get_all[T: Device](self, as_: type[T] = Device) -> list[T]:
        if self.integration is None:
            rows = self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices").fetchall()
        else:
            rows = (
                self._cursor().execute("SELECT data FROM devices WHERE integration = ?", (self.integration,)).fetchall()
            )
        return [as_.model_validate(json.loads(row["data"])) for row in rows]

    async def get[T: Device](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = Device) -> T | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def state[T: DeviceState](self, device_id: UUID, as_: type[T] = DeviceState) -> T | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        return as_.model_validate(record) if record else None

    async def get_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_id: UUID) -> ParameterState | None:
        record = self._record(device_id)
        if not record:
            return None
        return next(
            (ParameterState.model_validate(p) for p in record.get("parameters", []) if p["id"] == str(parameter_id)),
            None,
        )

    async def save(self, device: Device | DeviceState, previous_id: UUID | None = None):
        if self.integration is not None and device.integration != self.integration:
            raise PermissionError(f"Device {device.id} is outside integration scope {self.integration!r}")
        base: Record | None = None
        if previous_id is not None and previous_id != device.id:
            base = self._record(previous_id)
            self._cursor().execute("DELETE FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(previous_id),))
        self._write(merge(base if base is not None else self._record(device.id), device))

    async def save_parameter_state(self, device_id: UUID, parameter_state: ParameterState):
        record = self._record(device_id)
        if not record:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown or out-of-scope device {device_id}")
        updated = dump(parameter_state)
        record["parameters"] = [
            updated if p["id"] == str(parameter_state.id) else p for p in record.get("parameters", [])
        ]
        self._write(record)

    # Hub-internal (not on DeviceRepositoryProtocol); still scope-checked.

    async def update_parameter_visibility(self, parameter_id: UUID, visibility: ParameterVisibility):
        for device in await self.get_all():
            record = self._record(device.id)
            if not record:
                continue
            if any(p["id"] == str(parameter_id) for p in record.get("parameters", [])):
                for parameter in record["parameters"]:
                    if parameter["id"] == str(parameter_id):
                        parameter["visibility"] = visibility.value
                self._write(record)
                return

    async def delete(self, device_id: UUID):
        if self._record(device_id) is None:
            return
        self._cursor().execute("DELETE FROM devices WHERE uuid = ?", (str(device_id),))


__all__ = ["SqliteDeviceRepository"]

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/defaults.py

"""What a runtime runs by default, given explicitly: the defaults keep a composition root short and replaceable. Each
call builds new ones, so no two runtimes share a peripheral.

Under the Hub, hardware first (the order given is the order of preference)::

    Runtime(data, [Pinned(*mine), FixedPeripherals(*soldered), *default_peripherals(), *integrations], platform=...)

In library mode, one integration with what it needs::

    Runtime(data, [*default_peripherals(), HueController(platform)], platform=platform)
    Runtime(data, [HostNetwork(), ZeroconfDiscoveryService(), HueController(platform)], platform=platform)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import functools
import logging

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.host import BluetoothAdapters, HostNetwork
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.usb import UsbScanner
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ssdp import SSDPDiscoveryService
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.builtin import otbr, silabs_multiprotocol
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose import Compose

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def default_peripherals(*, listen_address: str = "127.0.0.1") -> list[Peripheral]:
    """Everything the SDK runs around integrations, in the order it binds: the sticks plugged in (by
    `default_usb_drivers`) before the containers that serve over them, Docker Compose that runs those, the
    multiprotocol border router before the standalone one, the Bluetooth router before the integrations, so it takes
    every adapter. On-demand ones run only while used. The containers on the host network answer on
    ``listen_address`` (`Compose`): the hub only by default."""
    zeroconf = _zeroconf()
    return [
        UsbScanner(),
        BluetoothAdapters(),
        HostNetwork(),
        Compose(listen_address),
        silabs_multiprotocol(),
        otbr(),
        BLEService(),
        *([zeroconf()] if zeroconf else []),
        SSDPDiscoveryService(),
    ]


@functools.cache  # said once
def _zeroconf() -> type[Peripheral] | None:
    try:
        from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.zeroconf import ZeroconfDiscoveryService
    except ImportError:
        log.warning('No DNS-SD without zeroconf: pip install "majordom-integration-sdk[discovery]"')
        return None
    return ZeroconfDiscoveryService


__all__ = ["default_peripherals"]

"""The one ``output`` every peripheral of a runtime shares."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import UUID

from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.output import ControllerOutput, IntegrationError
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Discovery
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.event import Event
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.notification import Notification

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from majordom_integration_sdk.controller.abstract_controller import AbstractController
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.runtime import Runtime


class HostOutput(ControllerOutput):
    """What every peripheral of a runtime tells, as its ``output``: its lifecycle goes to the runtime, a controller's
    reports to ``controller_output`` (the Hub). A controller that can't go on (an error not ``is_still_running``)
    fails in the runtime too, and one that changed what it provides has the runtime read it again."""

    def __init__(self, runtime: Runtime, controller_output: ControllerOutput):
        self.runtime, self.controller_output = runtime, controller_output

    # PeripheralOutput

    async def peripheral_did_change_provided(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_change_provided(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_learn(self, peripheral: Peripheral, facts: Mapping[str, Any]):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_learn(peripheral, facts)

    async def peripheral_did_stop(self, peripheral: Peripheral):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_stop(peripheral)

    async def peripheral_did_fail(self, peripheral: Peripheral, reason: str):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_fail(peripheral, reason)

    # ControllerOutput

    async def controller_did_receive_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery: Discovery):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_receive_discovery(controller, discovery)

    async def controller_did_update_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery: Discovery):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_update_discovery(controller, discovery)

    async def controller_did_lose_discovery(self, controller: AbstractController, discovery_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_lose_discovery(controller, discovery_id)

    async def controller_did_connect_device(self, controller: AbstractController, device_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_connect_device(controller, device_id)

    async def controller_did_lose_device(self, controller: AbstractController, device_id: UUID):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_lose_device(controller, device_id)

    async def controller_did_receive_events(self, controller: AbstractController, events: Iterable[Event]):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_receive_events(controller, events)

    async def controller_did_encounter_error(self, controller: AbstractController, error: IntegrationError):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_encounter_error(controller, error)
        if not error.is_still_running:
            await self.runtime.peripheral_did_fail(controller, error.message)

    async def controller_did_resolve_error(self, controller: AbstractController, error_id: str):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_resolve_error(controller, error_id)

    async def controller_did_emit_notification(self, controller: AbstractController, notification: Notification):
        await self.controller_output.controller_did_emit_notification(controller, notification)

    async def controller_did_change_provided(self, controller: AbstractController):
        await self.runtime.peripheral_did_change_provided(controller)

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/hardware/drivers.py

"""The SDK's USB drivers, for radios: recognise which firmware a stick runs, say what each firmware serves, flash
between them."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import hashlib
import re
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import ClassVar

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Endpoint, UsbDriver


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Firmware:
    url: str
    sha256: str
    is_stable: bool = False  # verified for shipping; the rest is offered on the dev channel only


_NABUCASA = "https://github.com/NabuCasa/silabs-firmware-builder/releases/download"


class Silabs(UsbDriver):
    """Silicon Labs EFR32 sticks: Zigbee NCP (EZSP), Thread RCP (Spinel) or multi-PAN RCP (CPC)."""

    name = "silabs"
    firmwares = {
        "zigbee-ncp": [Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "{device}", params={"baud": 115200, "flow_control": True})],
        "thread-rcp": [Endpoint("thread", "spinel", "{device}", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})],
        "multipan-rcp": [Endpoint("multipan", "silabs-cpc", "{device}", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})],
    }

    #: Builds per board, keyed by the product name in the stick's /dev/serial/by-id path.
    boards: ClassVar[dict[str, dict[str, Firmware]]] = {
        "SkyConnect": {
            "zigbee-ncp": Firmware(
                f"{_NABUCASA}/v2025.11.24/skyconnect_zigbee_ncp_7.4.4.5.gbl",
                "9a189c5797ee4ac975c0a5ebdd96b126332ac348cab27d065bd58e993e7bb7b0",
            ),
            "thread-rcp": Firmware(
                f"{_NABUCASA}/v2025.11.24/skyconnect_openthread_rcp_2.4.4.0_GitHub-7074a43e4_gsdk_4.4.4.gbl",
                "4cb5d04f4fab827745665104110fe1d272e4eb9bc38d1f496abb0311ef76e062",
            ),
            "multipan-rcp": Firmware(
                f"{_NABUCASA}/v2024.8.20/skyconnect_rcp-uart-802154_gsdk_4.4.4.gbl",
                "2140cfb06d2957e610057888a80fa068cf1bdacdbadb51ba430e2c8e1907a8bb",
            ),
        },
    }

    # NabuCasa's multi-PAN RCP is 802.15.4 only: none of these builds serves Bluetooth (``bluetooth`` stays empty)
    _apps = {"EZSP": "zigbee-ncp", "SPINEL": "thread-rcp", "CPC": "multipan-rcp"}

    async def identify(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        found = re.search(r"Detected ApplicationType\.(\w+)", await _flasher(path, "probe"))
        return self._apps.get(found[1]) if found else None

    def flashable(self, path: str, channel: str) -> list[str]:
        builds = next((b for name, b in self.boards.items() if name in path), {})
        return [fw for fw, build in builds.items() if build.is_stable or channel == "dev"]

    async def flash(self, path: str, firmware: str, channel: str, cache: Path):
        if firmware not in self.flashable(path, channel):
            raise ValueError(f"No {firmware} firmware for {path} on the {channel} channel")
        build = next(b[firmware] for name, b in self.boards.items() if name in path)
        file = cache / build.url.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
        if not file.exists():
            cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            data = await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: urllib.request.urlopen(build.url, timeout=60).read())
            if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != build.sha256:
                raise ValueError(f"Checksum mismatch for {build.url}")
            file.write_bytes(data)
        await _flasher(path, "flash", "--firmware", str(file))


class ZWave(UsbDriver):
    """Z-Wave controllers speaking the Serial API (any vendor)."""

    name = "zwave"
    firmwares = {
        "serial-api": [Endpoint("zwave", "serial-api", "{device}", params={"baud": 115200, "flow_control": False})]
    }

    async def identify(self, path: str) -> str | None:
        return "serial-api" if await asyncio.to_thread(_zwave_answers, path) else None


def _zwave_answers(path: str) -> bool:
    import serial  # the runtime extra

    # Serial API request frame for FUNC_ID_ZW_GET_VERSION: SOF, length, REQ, 0x15, checksum.
    # A controller replies with its library version string, "Z-Wave x.y", and repeats any reply
    # the host didn't ACK (answering CAN to new requests meanwhile): NAK first, ACK the answer.
    with serial.Serial(path, 115200, timeout=1) as port:
        port.write(b"\x15")
        for _ in range(3):
            port.reset_input_buffer()
            port.write(bytes([0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0x15, 0xE9]))
            if b"Z-Wave" in port.read(64):
                port.write(b"\x06")
                return True
    return False


async def _flasher(path: str, *args: str) -> str:
    """Run universal-silabs-flasher (an external tool, kept out of this package's dependencies)."""
    process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        "universal-silabs-flasher", "--device", path, *args,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
    )  # fmt: skip
    output = (await process.communicate())[0].decode(errors="replace")
    if process.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"universal-silabs-flasher {args[0]} failed on {path}:\n{output[-2000:]}")
    return output


#: USB ids of radios opened unasked to identify them. Generic bridges common on other boards stay out
#: (CH340 1a86:7523 on Arduinos, Espressif 303a on ESP32s): opening their port resets the board.
#: A device that isn't listed is identified only when asked (`Radio.probe`).
RADIO_USB_IDS = {
    ("10c4", "ea60"),  # CP210x: Home Assistant SkyConnect / ZBT-1, Sonoff ZBDongle-P and Z-Wave PZG23, Zooz ZST10
    ("10c4", "8a2a"),  # Nortek HUSBZB-1
    ("1a86", "55d4"),  # CH9102: Sonoff ZBDongle-E, SMLIGHT SLZB-07
    ("0658", "0200"),  # Sigma Designs: Aeotec Z-Stick, HomeSeer SmartStick
    ("1cf1", "0030"),  # dresden elektronik ConBee II
    ("0403", "6015"),  # FTDI X: ConBee III, ZiGate+
    ("0451", "16a8"),  # TI CC2531
}


def default_usb_drivers() -> list[UsbDriver]:
    """Every driver of the SDK, tried in this order on every unidentified stick: the cheap single-frame Z-Wave check
    first."""
    return [ZWave(), Silabs()]

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/hardware/fixed.py

"""Hardware soldered on the board, as peripherals."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Peripheral, UsbDriver
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.drivers import default_usb_drivers
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.usb import Radio


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FixedRadio:
    """A radio wired to the board: used without asking, by the driver named ``driver``. With no ``firmware`` that
    driver identifies it; ``params`` override the firmware's serial settings where the board wires them otherwise."""

    name: str
    path: str
    driver: str
    firmware: str | None = None
    params: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


class FixedPeripherals(Peripheral):
    """What is soldered on the board, as its owner describes it (the Hub reads its board profile): each one whose path
    exists is brought along, a radio as a `Radio`.

        FixedPeripherals(FixedRadio("mg26", "/dev/ttyAMA3", "silabs", "multipan-rcp", {"flow_control": False}))
    """

    name = "board"

    def __init__(self, *radios: FixedRadio, drivers: Sequence[UsbDriver] | None = None):
        self.radios, self.drivers = radios, default_usb_drivers() if drivers is None else list(drivers)
        self._present: list[Radio] = []

    @property
    def provides(self) -> list[Radio]:
        return self._present

    async def start(self):
        drivers = {driver.name: driver for driver in self.drivers}
        present = []
        for fixed in self.radios:
            if not Path(fixed.path).exists():
                continue
            driver = drivers[fixed.driver]
            known = driver if fixed.firmware else None
            radio = Radio(fixed.name, fixed.path, lambda driver=driver: [driver], known, fixed.firmware, fixed.params)
            await (radio.check_bluetooth() if known else radio.recognise())
            present.append(radio)
        self._present = present

    async def stop(self):
        self._present = []

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/hardware/host.py

"""What the host itself serves: its network and its Bluetooth adapters."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from glob import glob
from pathlib import Path

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Endpoint, Peripheral

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

POLL = 2  # seconds between looks at the adapters there are


class HostNetwork(Peripheral):
    """The host's IP network, shared by everything that talks over it: ``ip``."""

    name = "host"
    provides = [Endpoint("ip", is_shared=True)]


class BluetoothAdapters(Peripheral):
    """Every Bluetooth adapter of the host as its own single-use ``ble/bluez`` endpoint, with its ``index`` (the router
    takes them all when it is given first); off Linux, bleak's default adapter on the OS's own stack. Adapters that
    appear or disappear are followed."""

    name = "bluetooth-adapters"

    def __init__(self):
        self._adapters: list[str] = []
        self._watcher: asyncio.Task | None = None

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return [Endpoint("ble", "bluez", name, params={"index": name.removeprefix("hci")}) for name in self._adapters]

    async def start(self):
        self._adapters = _adapters()
        self._watcher = asyncio.create_task(self._watch(), name="bluetooth-adapters.watch")

    async def stop(self):
        if self._watcher:
            self._watcher.cancel()
        self._adapters = []

    async def _watch(self):
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(POLL)
            if (found := _adapters()) != self._adapters:
                self._adapters = found
                try:
                    await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)
                except Exception:
                    log.exception("Following the Bluetooth adapters failed")


def _adapters() -> list[str]:
    if sys.platform != "linux":
        return [""]
    return sorted(Path(path).name for path in glob("/sys/class/bluetooth/hci*") if ":" not in Path(path).name)

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/hardware/usb.py

"""USB devices as peripherals: the scanner brings one `Radio` along per stick plugged in."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import errno
import fcntl
import logging
import os
import tempfile
from collections.abc import Callable, Coroutine, Mapping, Sequence
from glob import glob
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from majordom_integration_sdk.files import read_json, write_json
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import (
    USB_DRIVER,
    Endpoint,
    Need,
    Peripheral,
    PeripheralChange,
    UsbDriver,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.hardware.drivers import RADIO_USB_IDS, default_usb_drivers
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import cpc_hci

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PROBE_TIMEOUT = 60  # per driver: one that hangs (bellows resetting a busy port) is given up
POLL = 2  # seconds between looks at the sticks plugged in
FIRMWARE_CACHE = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "majordom-firmware"  # downloads are checked against their checksum
UNSEEN = "another program"  # one that locked a port: whether it let go shows only by opening it


class RadioBusy(RuntimeError):
    """The radio is being flashed or probed already: ask again once that is done."""


class Radio(Peripheral["Radio.Settings"]):
    """A radio, a USB stick or soldered on the board: it serves what its firmware does once a driver identified it, and
    nothing while another program holds it or it is being flashed. Flashing, probing and forgetting it are the user's
    to ask for, one at a time: asked while one runs, they raise `RadioBusy`."""

    class Settings(BaseModel):
        firmware_channel: Literal["stable", "dev"] = Field(
            "stable", title="Radio firmware", description="Stable offers verified builds only, dev every known build."
        )

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        path: str,
        drivers: Callable[[], Sequence[UsbDriver]],
        driver: UsbDriver | None = None,
        firmware: str | None = None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,  # the firmware's serial settings, where soldered hardware wires them
        scanner: UsbScanner | None = None,  # what found it plugged in, which keeps what it is
    ):
        self.name, self.path, self.drivers, self.scanner = name, path, drivers, scanner
        self.driver, self.firmware, self.params = driver, firmware, params or {}
        self._given = driver, firmware  # what the board says a soldered one runs: kept if, forgotten, no driver tells
        self.found: dict[str, Any] = {}  # the serial settings its driver found it at, under the board's ``params``
        self.node = os.path.realpath(path)  # a container keeps the node it was created with: follow a re-enumeration
        self.held_by: str | None = None  # another program that has it open: left alone until probed
        self.is_claimed = False  # the user probed it: opened whoever holds it or whatever its USB id
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()  # held while it is flashed, probed or identified: one opens its port at a time
        self.has_bluetooth = False  # its multiprotocol firmware serves Bluetooth too
        self.settings = self.Settings()
        self._asked: list[UsbDriver] = []  # the drivers that didn't recognise it

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Radio({self.name!r}, {self.firmware!r})"

    @property
    def provides(self) -> list[Endpoint]:
        if self.is_busy or self.held_by or self.driver is None:
            return []
        endpoints = self.driver.serves(self.firmware, self.node, {**self.found, **self.params})
        if self.has_bluetooth:  # the multiprotocol container attaches it and tells its hciN
            endpoints.append(Endpoint("ble", "silabs-cpc-hci", self.node, params={"hci": None}))
        return endpoints

    @property
    def is_busy(self) -> bool:
        """Being flashed, probed or identified."""
        return self.lock.locked()

    @property
    def options(self) -> list[str]:
        """Firmwares it can be switched to on its channel."""
        return self.driver.flashable(self.path, self.settings.firmware_channel) if self.driver else []

    # Peripheral hooks

    async def settings_did_change(self, before: Radio.Settings) -> bool:
        """Its channel only changes what it may be flashed to: nothing restarts."""
        return True

    # Actions

    async def recognise(self, is_asking_again: bool = False):
        """Ask the drivers which firmware it runs, each once unless ``is_asking_again``, until one tells."""
        for driver in [d for d in self.drivers() if is_asking_again or all(d is not a for a in self._asked)]:
            if identified := await _identified(driver, self.path):
                self.driver, (self.firmware, self.found) = driver, identified
                await self.check_bluetooth()
                return
            self._asked.append(driver)
        log.info(f"No driver recognised {self.path}")

    async def probe(self):
        """Identify it now, also a stick no driver knows the USB id of, or one another program holds: its port is
        opened, which may reset what's behind it. Whatever uses it lets go of it first."""
        async with self._busy():
            self.held_by, self.is_claimed = None, True
            await self.recognise(is_asking_again=True)
            self._remember()

    async def flash(self, firmware: str):
        """Switch it to ``firmware`` on its channel; whatever uses it lets go of it first and gets it back after."""
        if (driver := self.driver) is None:
            raise LookupError(f"No driver knows {self.name}: probe it first")
        async with self._busy():
            try:
                await driver.flash(self.path, firmware, self.settings.firmware_channel, FIRMWARE_CACHE)
            finally:  # whether it took or not, what ran before may be gone
                self.firmware, self.found = await _identified(driver, self.path) or (None, {})
                self.has_bluetooth = False
                await self.check_bluetooth()
                self._remember()

    async def forget(self):
        """Forget what it is and that the user probed it: whatever uses it lets go of it, and it is looked at again as
        a stick plugged in anew, or, soldered, identified again: as the board says when no driver tells."""
        async with self._busy():
            if self.scanner:  # first: a scan going on would take it back from there
                self.scanner.forget(self)
            self.driver, self.firmware, self.found, self.has_bluetooth = None, None, {}, False
            self.is_claimed, self._asked = False, []
            if self.scanner is None:
                await self.recognise()
                if self.driver is None and self._given[1]:
                    self.driver, self.firmware = self._given
                    await self.check_bluetooth()
        if self.scanner:
            await self.scanner.rescan()

    async def check_bluetooth(self):
        """Whether a multi-PAN firmware serves Bluetooth too: the driver says where it knows, else it is asked."""
        endpoints = self.driver.serves(self.firmware, self.node) if self.driver else []
        if any(e.family == "multipan" for e in endpoints) and self.driver:
            self.has_bluetooth = self.firmware in self.driver.bluetooth or await cpc_hci.has_bluetooth(self.path)

    # Private

    def _remember(self):
        if self.scanner:
            self.scanner.remember(self)

    @contextlib.asynccontextmanager
    async def _busy(self):
        if self.lock.locked():
            raise RadioBusy(f"{self.name} is being flashed or probed: ask again once that is done")
        try:
            async with self.lock:
                await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)  # returns once what used it let go of it
                yield
        finally:
            await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)


class UsbScanner(Peripheral):
    """USB devices plugged in (``/dev/serial/by-id``), each brought along as a `Radio` and identified by its drivers,
    then by the ones integrations provide (``usb-driver``): radios today. Only a device whose USB id is a known
    radio's is opened unasked; another is identified when the user asks (`Radio.probe`). One another program holds is
    left alone until then. What it identified and what the user probed is remembered, in ``sticks.json`` of its data
    folder: a stick known from before isn't opened again, and waits for the driver that identified it (an
    integration's, bound once that runs).

        UsbScanner()  # every SDK driver: default_usb_drivers()
        UsbScanner(drivers=[Silabs()])
    """

    name = "usb"
    needs = [Need(USB_DRIVER, is_many=True, is_required=False)]

    def __init__(self, drivers: Sequence[UsbDriver] | None = None):
        self.drivers = default_usb_drivers() if drivers is None else list(drivers)
        self._radios: list[Radio] = []
        self._known: dict[str, Any] = {}  # by-id name -> what it was identified as, whether the user claimed it
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()  # watching the sticks, and asking new drivers about them
        self._scanning = asyncio.Lock()  # one scan at a time: two would open a stick at once

    @property
    def provides(self) -> list[Radio]:
        return self._radios

    @property
    def radios(self) -> list[Radio]:
        return list(self._radios)

    # Lifecycle

    async def start(self):
        self._known = read_json(self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "sticks.json")
        await self._scan()
        self._spawn(self._watch())

    async def stop(self):
        for task in self._tasks:
            task.cancel()
        self._radios = []

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        """A driver was bound, e.g. one an integration provides: it may know the sticks no other driver did. Asked in
        the background, as a probe may take long."""
        self._spawn(self.rescan())
        return True

    # Actions

    async def rescan(self):
        """Follow the sticks plugged in now, identifying the new ones it may open."""
        try:
            await self._scan()
            await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("Following the USB sticks failed")

    def remember(self, *radios: Radio):
        """Keep what ``radios`` are, and whether the user claimed them, across restarts."""
        for radio in radios:
            driver = radio.driver.name if radio.driver else None
            known = {
                "driver": driver,
                "firmware": radio.firmware,
                "params": radio.found,
                "has_bluetooth": radio.has_bluetooth,
            }
            self._known[radio.name] = known | {"is_claimed": radio.is_claimed}
        write_json(self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "sticks.json", self._known)

    def forget(self, radio: Radio):
        """Forget what ``radio`` is, and that the user claimed it: the next scan looks at it as a stick plugged in
        anew."""
        self._known.pop(radio.name, None)
        write_json(self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "sticks.json", self._known)

    # Private

    def _spawn(self, coroutine: Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]):
        task = asyncio.create_task(coroutine)
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)

    def _drivers(self) -> list[UsbDriver]:
        return [*self.drivers, *(endpoint.instance for endpoint in self.peripherals.endpoints(USB_DRIVER))]

    async def _scan(self):
        """Follow the sticks plugged in, and identify the new ones it may open."""
        async with self._scanning:
            radios = {radio.name: radio for radio in self.radios}
            found = _sticks()
            drivers = {driver.name for driver in self._drivers()}
            for name, path in found.items():
                radio = radios.get(name) or self._radio(name, path)
                if radio.driver is None:  # what identified it may only now be here: a driver an integration provides
                    self._restore(radio)
                radio.node = os.path.realpath(path)
                remembered = self._known.get(name, {}).get("driver")
                is_awaited = radio.driver is None and remembered is not None and remembered not in drivers
                is_trusted = (radio.is_claimed or _usb_id(path) in RADIO_USB_IDS) and not is_awaited
                if not radio.is_claimed and not radio.is_busy:
                    radio.held_by = _holder(path, is_opening_allowed=is_trusted and radio.driver is None)
                if is_trusted and radio.driver is None and not radio.held_by and not radio.is_busy:
                    async with radio.lock:
                        await radio.recognise()
                radios[name] = radio
            self._radios = [radios[name] for name in sorted(found)]
        self.remember(*[radio for radio in self._radios if radio.driver or radio.is_claimed])

    def _radio(self, name: str, path: str) -> Radio:
        """A stick plugged in, claimed if the user probed it before."""
        radio = Radio(name, path, self._drivers, scanner=self)
        radio.is_claimed = self._known.get(name, {}).get("is_claimed", False)
        return radio

    def _restore(self, radio: Radio):
        """What it was identified as before, once the driver that did is here."""
        known, drivers = self._known.get(radio.name, {}), {driver.name: driver for driver in self._drivers()}
        if (driver := drivers.get(known.get("driver", ""))) and (firmware := known.get("firmware")):
            radio.driver, radio.firmware, radio.has_bluetooth = driver, firmware, known.get("has_bluetooth", False)
            radio.found = known.get("params", {})

    async def _watch(self):
        seen = _nodes(_sticks())
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(POLL)
            found = _nodes(_sticks())
            if found != seen:  # act once the change held for one more poll (a stick re-enumerating)
                seen = found
                continue
            is_moved = found != {radio.name: radio.node for radio in self.radios}
            is_let_go = any(r.held_by not in (None, UNSEEN) and not _holder(r.path) for r in self.radios)
            if is_moved or is_let_go:
                await self.rescan()


async def _identified(driver: UsbDriver, path: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """What ``driver`` recognises the device at ``path`` running, and the serial settings it found it at; None when it
    doesn't, can't tell, or hangs."""
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(PROBE_TIMEOUT):
            found = await driver.identify(path)
    except Exception as error:
        log.warning(f"{driver.name} failed to identify {path}: {_failure(error)}")
        return None
    firmware, params = (found, {}) if isinstance(found, str) or found is None else found
    return (firmware, dict(params)) if firmware else None


def _failure(error: Exception) -> str:
    return str(error) or type(error).__name__


def _sticks() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {Path(path).name: path for path in glob("/dev/serial/by-id/*")}


def _nodes(paths: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The device node behind each path. After a USB reset a stick keeps its by-id name but may come back
    on another tty; a container keeps the node it was created with, which may then be another device."""
    return {name: os.path.realpath(path) for name, path in paths.items()}


def _usb_id(path: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """USB vendor and product id of the device behind a serial port; None for a UART."""
    device = Path("/sys/class/tty", Path(os.path.realpath(path)).name, "device").resolve()
    for parent in (device, *device.parents):
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            return (parent / "idVendor").read_text().strip(), (parent / "idProduct").read_text().strip()
    return None


def _holder(path: str, is_opening_allowed: bool = False) -> str | None:
    """The other program that has a serial port open: one whose open files we may read, or with
    ``is_opening_allowed`` (it opens the port) one that locked it, whoever runs it (`UNSEEN`). Our own containers see
    the port under another name (/dev/ttyRCP), so they don't count."""
    names = {path, os.path.realpath(path)}
    for fd in glob("/proc/[0-9]*/fd/*"):
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            if (pid := fd.split("/")[2]) != str(os.getpid()) and os.readlink(fd) in names:
                return Path(f"/proc/{pid}/comm").read_text().strip()
    if not is_opening_allowed:
        return None
    try:
        port = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOCTTY | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    except OSError as error:
        return UNSEEN if error.errno == errno.EBUSY else None  # EBUSY: opened exclusively (TIOCEXCL)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(port, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)  # pyserial's and node-serialport's exclusive lock
    except OSError:
        return UNSEEN
    finally:
        os.close(port)
    return None

"""Endpoints you provide yourself."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence

from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import Endpoint, Peripheral


class Pinned(Peripheral):
    """Endpoints you run yourself, one per family: a ``socket://`` EZSP stick on the network, a matter-server of your
    own. Give it to the runtime first, so they win over anything found.

        stick = Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "socket://192.168.1.5:6638")
        Runtime(data, [Pinned(stick), *default_peripherals()], platform=platform)
    """

    name = "pinned"

    def __init__(self, *endpoints: Endpoint):
        self._endpoints = {endpoint.family: endpoint for endpoint in endpoints}

    @property
    def provides(self) -> Sequence[Endpoint]:
        return list(self._endpoints.values())

    async def pin(self, endpoint: Endpoint):
        """Provide ``endpoint`` for its family, in place of the one pinned before."""
        self._endpoints[endpoint.family] = endpoint
        await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)

    async def unpin(self, family: str):
        self._endpoints.pop(family, None)
        await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)

# FILE: majordom_integration_sdk/runtime/peripherals/providers/ble/bluez.py
================================================================================
"""The host's Bluetooth adapters as ble/bluez sources of the router, through bleak (BlueZ on Linux, the OS's own
stack elsewhere), and pairing through BlueZ with an agent of our own, scoped to the one device being paired.

LE Secure Connections "Just Works" still asks the host to confirm (the kernel's confirm hint), and bluetoothd turns that
into an agent call: without an agent the pairing fails ("Numeric comparison failed"), and bleak registers none. So the
pairing is started from a D-Bus connection that holds an `org.bluez.Agent1` (bluetoothd asks the agent of whoever called
`Pair`): it confirms only that device, and goes away with the connection.
"""

import asyncio
import contextlib
import itertools
import logging
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

from bleak import BleakClient, BleakScanner
from bleak.args.bluez import OrPattern
from bleak.assigned_numbers import AdvertisementDataType
from bleak.backends.device import BLEDevice
from bleak.backends.scanner import AdvertisementData
from bleak.exc import BleakError

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities.ble import (
    BLEConnection,
    BLEPairingError,
    GattCharacteristic,
    GattService,
    OnAdvertisement,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

AGENT_PATH = "/io/majordom/pairing_agent"
REJECTED = "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"
_agents = itertools.count()

Answer = tuple[str, list[Any]] | str  # (signature, body) to return, or the name of the error to raise


def agent_answer(member: str, body: list[Any], device_path: str) -> Answer:
    """What the agent answers bluetoothd's ``member`` call; anything not about ``device_path`` is refused."""
    if member in ("Release", "Cancel"):
        return "", []
    if not body or body[0] != device_path:
        return REJECTED
    if member in ("RequestAuthorization", "RequestConfirmation"):  # Just Works: nothing to compare without a display
        return "", []
    return REJECTED  # passkeys and PIN codes (BR/EDR), service authorization, displays we don't have


def device_path(adapter: str, address: str) -> str:
    return f"/org/bluez/{adapter}/dev_{address.upper().replace(':', '_')}"


async def pair_through_agent(adapter: str, address: str):
    """Pairs the connected device ``address`` on ``adapter`` (hci0, …); raises `ConnectionError` with BlueZ's error."""
    # bleak's BlueZ backend brings dbus-fast, on Linux only
    from dbus_fast import BusType, Message, MessageType
    from dbus_fast.aio import MessageBus

    path, agent = device_path(adapter, address), f"{AGENT_PATH}{next(_agents)}"

    def on_message(message: Message) -> Message | None:
        if message.message_type != MessageType.METHOD_CALL or message.path != agent:
            return None
        answer = agent_answer(message.member or "", list(message.body), path)
        if isinstance(answer, str):
            return Message.new_error(message, answer, "Not the device being paired")
        return Message.new_method_return(message, *answer)

    async def call(message: Message):
        reply = await bus.call(message)
        if reply is not None and reply.message_type == MessageType.ERROR:
            raise ConnectionError(f"{reply.error_name}: {' '.join(map(str, reply.body))}".strip(": "))

    bus = await MessageBus(bus_type=BusType.SYSTEM).connect()
    bus.add_message_handler(on_message)
    try:
        manager = {"destination": "org.bluez", "path": "/org/bluez", "interface": "org.bluez.AgentManager1"}
        await call(Message(**manager, member="RegisterAgent", signature="os", body=[agent, "NoInputNoOutput"]))
        try:
            await call(Message(destination="org.bluez", path=path, interface="org.bluez.Device1", member="Pair"))
        except ConnectionError as e:
            if not str(e).startswith("org.bluez.Error.AlreadyExists"):  # paired already: the link is encrypted
                raise
        finally:
            with contextlib.suppress(ConnectionError):
                await call(Message(**manager, member="UnregisterAgent", signature="o", body=[agent]))
    finally:
        bus.disconnect()


_EVERY_ADVERTISER = [OrPattern(0, AdvertisementDataType.FLAGS, flags) for flags in (b"\x02", b"\x06", b"\x1a")]


class LocalAdapter:
    """A Bluetooth adapter of this machine, through bleak (BlueZ on Linux)."""

    is_pairable = True  # LE Secure Connections where the device offers it; through a scoped BlueZ agent on Linux

    def __init__(self, adapter: str | None = None):
        self.name = adapter or "local"
        self._options = {"bluez": {"adapter": adapter}} if adapter else {}
        self._scanner: BleakScanner | None = None
        self._devices: dict[str, BLEDevice] = {}  # address -> last seen; connecting by it skips a scan
        self.is_passive = False  # set: a passive scan of every advertiser, the listeners' matchers choose
        self._is_passive_refused = False
        self._on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement | None = None
        self._scan_lock = asyncio.Lock()  # a connect holds it: no scan starts until it ends

    async def set_scan_mode(self, is_active: bool):
        if self.is_passive == (not is_active):
            return
        self.is_passive = not is_active
        if self._scanner and self._on_advertisement:  # scanning: again, in the new mode
            await self.stop()
            await self.start(self._on_advertisement)

    async def start(self, on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement):
        self._on_advertisement = on_advertisement

        def on_detection(device: BLEDevice, adv_data: AdvertisementData):
            self._devices.pop(device.address, None)  # re-added last: the dict stays oldest first
            self._devices[device.address] = device
            if len(self._devices) > 1024:  # phones rotate their address: drop the oldest
                del self._devices[next(iter(self._devices))]
            on_advertisement(device, adv_data)

        # BlueZ refuses a passive scan without --experimental (Raspberry Pi OS's default): then it scans actively. With
        # it, a Pi 5 (BlueZ 5.82, no offload) passes adverts only through patterns on the flags (2026-10-14), as in HA.
        async with self._scan_lock:
            if self.is_passive and not self._is_passive_refused:
                bluez = {**self._options.get("bluez", {}), "or_patterns": _EVERY_ADVERTISER}
                try:  # macOS refuses a passive scan already when the scanner is made
                    self._scanner = BleakScanner(detection_callback=on_detection, scanning_mode="passive", bluez=bluez)
                    return await self._scanner.start()
                except Exception as e:
                    # BlueZ's advertisement monitor is missing (an old or non-experimental bluetoothd)
                    logger.warning(f"BLE {self.name} can't scan passively, scanning actively: {e}")
                    self._is_passive_refused = True
            self.is_passive = False
            self._scanner = BleakScanner(detection_callback=on_detection, **self._options)
            await self._scanner.start()

    async def stop(self):
        async with self._scan_lock:
            scanner, self._scanner = self._scanner, None
            if scanner:
                await scanner.stop()

    async def connect(self, address: str, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None]) -> BLEConnection:
        device = self._devices.get(address, address)
        client = BleakClient(device, disconnected_callback=lambda _: on_disconnect(), **self._options)
        async with self._scan_lock:
            scanner = self._scanner
            if scanner:  # many adapters (the Raspberry Pi's included) stall a connect while discovering
                await scanner.stop()
            try:
                await client.connect()
            finally:
                if scanner:
                    await scanner.start()
        return _BleakConnection(client, self._options.get("bluez", {}).get("adapter") or "hci0")


class _BleakConnection:
    def __init__(self, client: BleakClient, adapter: str):
        self._client, self._adapter = client, adapter

    @property
    def mtu(self) -> int:
        # On BlueZ bleak says 23 until the MTU is acquired, though BlueZ exchanged the real one on connect and every
        # characteristic carries it; Matter's BTP sized its segments by the 23 and ran ~10x slower (2026-10-22).
        characteristics = self._client.services.characteristics.values()
        return max((c.max_write_without_response_size + 3 for c in characteristics), default=self._client.mtu_size)

    async def services(self) -> list[GattService]:
        return [
            GattService(
                service.uuid,
                service.handle,
                tuple(GattCharacteristic(c.uuid, c.handle, tuple(c.properties)) for c in service.characteristics),
            )
            for service in self._client.services
        ]

    async def read(self, handle: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes(await self._client.read_gatt_char(handle))

    async def write(self, handle: int, data: bytes, is_response_needed: bool = True):
        await self._client.write_gatt_char(handle, data, response=is_response_needed)

    async def start_notify(self, handle: int, callback: Callable[[bytes], None]):
        await self._client.start_notify(handle, lambda _, data: callback(bytes(data)))

    async def stop_notify(self, handle: int):
        await self._client.stop_notify(handle)

    async def pair(self):
        try:
            if sys.platform == "linux":  # bleak's pair() brings no agent: LE Secure Connections fails without one
                await pair_through_agent(self._adapter, self._client.address)
            else:  # the OS pairs on its own, with its own prompts
                await self._client.pair()
        except (ConnectionError, BleakError, EOFError) as e:  # org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed, a dropped link
            raise BLEPairingError(f"Pairing failed: {e}") from e

    async def unpair(self):
        await self._client.unpair()

    async def disconnect(self):
        await self._client.disconnect()
