"""Every row of the peripheral state machine, the one lifetime rule, retries and readiness."""

import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import replace
from typing import Any

import pytest

from support import changed, run, settle, state, until

from majordom_integration_sdk import STABLE_RUN, Endpoint, Need, NoSettings, PeripheralChange, Platform
from majordom_integration_sdk import SettingsExtraField as Extra
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import MemoryDisabledStore, PeripheralStatus, Runtime
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralState as S
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import StatusKind as K
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import runtime as module
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakePeripheral, RecordingRuntimeOutput, build_test_platform

ZIGBEE = Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB0")
MOVED = Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB1")
THREAD = Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", "http://127.0.0.1:8081", is_shared=True)
SERVER = Endpoint("matter", "matter-server", "ws://127.0.0.1:5580", is_shared=True)
UNBOUND = "need zigbee/*: nothing offers it"


def radio(*provides: Endpoint) -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("radio", provides=provides)


def zigbee(**kwargs) -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")], **kwargs)

async def test_a_peripheral_with_nothing_to_wait_for_runs_and_stops_with_the_runtime(tmp_path):
    host = FakePeripheral("host", provides=[Endpoint("ip", is_shared=True)])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, host)
    assert runtime.status(host) == PeripheralStatus(S.RUNNING)

    await runtime.stop()
    assert host.calls == ["start", "stop"]


async def test_what_it_runs_is_known_before_it_starts(tmp_path):
    host, hue = FakePeripheral("host"), FakePeripheral("hue")
    runtime = Runtime(tmp_path / "data", [host], platform=build_test_platform(tmp_path))
    await runtime.add(hue)  # library mode: given one by one
    assert runtime.peripherals == [host, hue] and runtime.status(hue) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING)
    assert hue.calls == [] and hue.platform is runtime.platform

    await runtime.remove(host)
    assert runtime.peripherals == [hue] and host.calls == []


async def test_boot_without_a_required_need_waits_and_says_why(tmp_path):
    output = RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    integration = zigbee()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration, output=output)

    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, UNBOUND)
    assert runtime.unbound(integration) == {"zigbee": UNBOUND}
    assert output.statuses == [("zigbee", PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, UNBOUND))]
    assert str(runtime.status(integration)) == f"waiting: {UNBOUND}"  # for logs and the CLI
    assert integration.calls == []


async def test_it_starts_once_its_need_appears_and_waits_again_while_it_is_lost(tmp_path):
    stick, integration = radio(), zigbee()
    output = RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration, output=output)

    stick.provided = [ZIGBEE]  # identified
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING
    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == ZIGBEE
    assert runtime.providers(integration) == {"zigbee": "radio"}
    assert [status.state for name, status in output.statuses if name == "zigbee"] == [S.WAITING, S.STARTING, S.RUNNING]

    stick.provided = []  # unplugged
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, UNBOUND)
    assert integration.changes == []  # a lost required need stops it without asking

    stick.provided = [ZIGBEE]  # plugged in again
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING
    assert integration.calls == ["start", "stop", "start"]


# running: what moved


async def test_a_moved_need_is_handed_over_or_restarts_it(tmp_path):
    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), zigbee(answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)

    stick.provided = [MOVED]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert integration.changes == [PeripheralChange("zigbee", ZIGBEE, MOVED)]
    assert integration.calls == ["start"]  # handled in place
    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == MOVED  # already there when it heard

    integration.answer = False
    stick.provided = [ZIGBEE]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert integration.calls == ["start", "stop", "start"]
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING


async def test_an_optional_need_lost_or_back_is_handed_over(tmp_path):
    border = FakePeripheral("otbr", provides=[THREAD])
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", is_required=False)], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, border, matter)

    await runtime.disable(border)
    await settle(runtime)
    appeared = PeripheralChange("thread", None, THREAD)  # it started beside the border router, at boot
    assert matter.changes == [appeared, PeripheralChange("thread", THREAD, None)]
    assert state(runtime, matter) == S.RUNNING
    assert runtime.unbound(matter) == {"thread": "need thread/*: otbr is disabled"}

    await runtime.enable(border)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert matter.changes == [appeared, PeripheralChange("thread", THREAD, None), appeared]
    assert matter.calls == ["start"]


async def test_a_hook_that_hangs_times_out(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "HOOK_TIMEOUT", 0.01)

    class Hangs(FakePeripheral):
        async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change):
            await asyncio.Event().wait()

    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), Hangs("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    stick.provided = [MOVED]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    expected = PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.RETRYING, "didn't take the change within 0.01 s; trying again in 0.01 s")
    assert runtime.status(integration) == expected


async def test_a_hook_that_raises_restarts_it_through_the_retries(tmp_path):
    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), zigbee(answer=RuntimeError("confused"))
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)

    stick.provided = [MOVED]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.RETRYING, "confused; trying again in 0.01 s")

async def test_a_hook_cancelled_from_inside_is_a_failure_and_the_others_hear_on(tmp_path):
    class Cancelled(FakePeripheral):
        async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before):
            raise asyncio.CancelledError  # e.g. a call it awaited lost its server

    cancelled, after = Cancelled("matter"), FakePeripheral("after", answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, cancelled, after)
    before = runtime.platform
    await runtime.update_platform(replace(before, region="Europe"))
    assert runtime.status(cancelled) == PeripheralStatus(
        S.WAITING, K.RETRYING, "CancelledError; trying again in 0.01 s"
    )
    assert after.changes == [("platform", before)]


async def moves(runtime, stick: FakePeripheral, integration: FakePeripheral, times: int):
    """The stick moves ``times``, each once the integration runs again."""
    for endpoint in [MOVED, ZIGBEE] * times:
        await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING)
        stick.provided = [endpoint]
        await changed(runtime, stick)
        times -= 1
        if not times:
            return


async def test_hook_failures_in_a_row_give_it_up(tmp_path):
    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), zigbee(answer=RuntimeError("confused"))
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    await moves(runtime, stick, integration, len(module.RETRY_DELAYS) + 1)
    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(S.FAILED, K.GAVE_UP, "confused")


async def test_a_failure_after_a_stable_run_starts_the_retries_over(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "STABLE_RUN", 0)
    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), zigbee(answer=RuntimeError("confused"))
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    await moves(runtime, stick, integration, len(module.RETRY_DELAYS) + 1)
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.WAITING


def test_an_integration_holds_a_reconnect_as_long_as_the_runtime_holds_a_run():
    # its outage is over once a reconnect held a stable run: a server that drops every time is reported
    assert STABLE_RUN == module.STABLE_RUN == 300

async def test_a_start_that_raises_is_tried_again_then_given_up_on(tmp_path):
    output = RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    broken = FakePeripheral("broken", failures=10)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, broken, output=output)
    assert runtime.status(broken) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.RETRYING, "broken broke; trying again in 0.01 s")

    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, broken) == S.FAILED)
    assert runtime.status(broken) == PeripheralStatus(S.FAILED, K.GAVE_UP, "broken broke")
    assert broken.calls == ["start", "stop"] * 4  # the first, then one per retry delay; each releases what it holds
    assert output.last("broken") == PeripheralStatus(S.FAILED, K.GAVE_UP, "broken broke")

async def test_a_start_that_ignores_being_stopped_is_left_behind(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "STOP_TIMEOUT", 0.01)
    started = asyncio.Event()

    class Stubborn(FakePeripheral):
        async def start(self):
            await super().start()
            started.set()
            try:
                await asyncio.Event().wait()
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # goes on regardless

    stubborn = Stubborn("stubborn")
    runtime = Runtime(tmp_path / "data", [stubborn], platform=build_test_platform(tmp_path))

    await settle(runtime)
    assert state(runtime, stubborn) == S.DISABLED

async def test_a_failed_one_isnt_revived_by_a_replug_only_by_the_user(tmp_path):

# disabled


async def test_disabled_is_kept_and_never_revived_by_a_replug(tmp_path):
    store = MemoryDisabledStore()
    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), zigbee()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration, disabled=store)

    await runtime.disable(integration)
    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(S.DISABLED)
    assert integration.calls == ["start", "stop"]
    assert store.is_disabled("zigbee")
    stick.provided = []
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    stick.provided = [ZIGBEE]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.DISABLED
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="enable it"):
        await runtime.restart(integration)

    again = zigbee()  # after a reboot
    runtime = await run(tmp_path / "again", radio(ZIGBEE), again, disabled=store)
    assert state(runtime, again) == S.DISABLED and again.calls == []

    await runtime.enable(again)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert state(runtime, again) == S.RUNNING
    assert not store.is_disabled("zigbee")

# calls from what a peripheral runs in the background, and from the runtime's own output


async def test_a_call_from_a_task_a_start_spawned_returns_once_acted_on(tmp_path):
    seen: list[S] = []

    class Stick(FakePeripheral):
        async def start(self):
            await super().start()
            self.task = asyncio.create_task(self.flash_later())

        async def flash_later(self):
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
            self.provided = []  # busy: being flashed
            await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)
            seen.append(state(runtime, integration))

    stick, integration = Stick("stick", provides=[ZIGBEE]), zigbee()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    await stick.task
    assert seen == [S.WAITING]  # it let go of the stick before the flash goes on


async def test_a_call_from_a_task_a_hook_awaits_returns_at_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """A task a hook awaits counts as inside it (a TaskGroup reconnecting its nodes): the runtime acts once the hook
    returned, rather than the hook waiting on the runtime that waits on it."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "HOOK_TIMEOUT", 0.5)

    class Reconnects(FakePeripheral):
        async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change):
            async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
                group.create_task(self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self))
            return await super().needed_peripheral_did_change(change)

    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), Reconnects("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    stick.provided = [MOVED]
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert (runtime.status(integration), integration.calls) == (PeripheralStatus(S.RUNNING), ["start"])


async def test_a_call_from_a_task_a_stop_awaits_returns_at_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "STOP_TIMEOUT", 0.5)
    stopped: list[bool] = []

    class LetsGo(FakePeripheral):
        async def stop(self):
            await super().stop()
            await asyncio.gather(self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self))  # its nodes go, each telling
            stopped.append(True)

    integration = LetsGo("esphome")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)
    await runtime.disable(integration)
    assert stopped == [True]  # ran to its end, never cut short


async def test_a_call_scheduled_by_a_status_callback_returns_once_acted_on(tmp_path):
    seen: list[S] = []
    integration, ran = FakePeripheral("zigbee"), asyncio.Event()

    class Output(RecordingRuntimeOutput):
        def peripheral_did_change_status(self, peripheral, status):
            super().peripheral_did_change_status(peripheral, status)
            if status.state == S.RUNNING:
                self.task = asyncio.ensure_future(disable())

    async def disable():
        await ran.wait()
        await runtime.disable(integration)
        seen.append(state(runtime, integration))

    output = Output()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration, output=output)
    ran.set()
    await output.task
    assert seen == [S.DISABLED]


async def test_a_call_scheduled_from_what_a_starts_task_set_off_returns_once_acted_on(tmp_path):
    """The runtime's own work is inside no peripheral's call, though a task of one's start set it off: what its owner
    schedules from there waits like any other caller."""
    seen: list[S] = []
    integration, released = zigbee(), asyncio.Event()

    class Brings(FakePeripheral):
        async def start(self):
            await super().start()
            async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as group:
                group.create_task(self.bring())
            await released.wait()

        async def bring(self):
            self.provided = [ZIGBEE]
            await self.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(self)

    class Output(RecordingRuntimeOutput):
        def peripheral_did_change_status(self, peripheral, status):
            super().peripheral_did_change_status(peripheral, status)
            if peripheral is integration and status.kind == K.NEEDS_STARTING:
                self.task = asyncio.ensure_future(disable())

    async def disable():
        await runtime.disable(integration)
        seen.append(state(runtime, integration))

    output = Output()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Brings("stick"), integration, output=output, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: hasattr(output, "task"), settled=False)
    await output.task
    released.set()
    assert seen == [S.DISABLED]


class Keeper(FakePeripheral):
    """Keeps a connection in a task of its own, which tells the runtime it can't go on; its stop cancels that task
    and waits for it, as a controller's does."""

    def __init__(self, tell: Callable[[FakePeripheral], Awaitable[Any]]):
        super().__init__("keeper")
        self.tell = tell

    async def start(self):
        await super().start()
        self.keeper = asyncio.create_task(self.keep())

    async def keep(self):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        if len(self.calls) == 1:
            await self.tell(self)

    async def stop(self):
        await super().stop()
        self.keeper.cancel()
        await asyncio.wait([self.keeper])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("tell", "status"),
    [
        (lambda p: p.output.peripheral_did_fail(p, "Lost the server."), PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.RETRYING)),
        (lambda p: p.output.peripheral_did_stop(p), PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.STOPPED_ITSELF)),
    ],
)
async def test_one_that_tells_from_its_own_task_is_stopped_in_the_runtimes(tmp_path, tell, status):
    keeper = Keeper(tell)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, keeper)
    await asyncio.wait([keeper.keeper])
    await settle(runtime)
    assert (keeper.calls, runtime.status(keeper).state, runtime.status(keeper).kind) == (
        ["start", "stop"],
        status.state,
        status.kind,
    )
    assert keeper.keeper.cancelled()  # its stop ended the task that told


async def test_a_pass_a_call_set_off_goes_on_when_the_caller_is_cancelled(tmp_path):
    heard, release = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()

    class Slow(FakePeripheral):
        async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change):
            heard.set()
            await release.wait()
            return await super().needed_peripheral_did_change(change)

    stick, integration = radio(ZIGBEE), Slow("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, stick, integration)
    stick.provided = [MOVED]
    caller = asyncio.create_task(stick.output.peripheral_did_change_provided(stick))  # e.g. a node's connection
    await heard.wait()
    caller.cancel()  # e.g. the node was unpaired meanwhile
    release.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert integration.changes == [PeripheralChange("zigbee", ZIGBEE, MOVED)]  # the hook ran to its end
    assert (state(runtime, integration), integration.calls) == (S.RUNNING, ["start"])


# a server next to what needs it, and what a peripheral brings along while it runs


def matter_and_server() -> tuple[FakePeripheral, FakePeripheral]:
    return FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("matter")]), FakePeripheral(
        "matter-server", provides=[SERVER], is_on_demand=True
    )


async def test_a_server_runs_while_what_needs_it_runs(tmp_path):
    matter, server = matter_and_server()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, server, matter)
    assert (state(runtime, matter), state(runtime, server)) == (S.RUNNING, S.RUNNING)

    await runtime.disable(matter)
    assert server.calls == ["start", "stop"]
    assert runtime.status(server) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.UNUSED, "nothing that runs uses it")

    await runtime.enable(matter)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert (state(runtime, matter), state(runtime, server)) == (S.RUNNING, S.RUNNING)


async def test_a_server_only_a_failed_one_needs_stops(tmp_path):
    matter, server = matter_and_server()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, server, matter)
    for _ in range(len(module.RETRY_DELAYS) + 1):
        await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, matter) == S.RUNNING)
        await matter.output.peripheral_did_fail(matter, "gave up")
    assert runtime.status(server) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.UNUSED, "nothing that runs uses it")


async def test_what_it_brought_along_while_running_goes_when_it_stops(tmp_path):
    esphome = FakePeripheral("esphome")
    proxy = FakePeripheral("esphome:aa", provides=[Endpoint("ble", "esphome-proxy", "esphome:aa")])
    router = FakePeripheral("router", [Need("ble", ["esphome-proxy"], is_many=True, is_required=False)], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, router, esphome)

    esphome.provided.append(proxy)  # a node connected
    await changed(runtime, esphome)
    assert state(runtime, proxy) == S.RUNNING
    assert router.peripherals.endpoints("ble") == list(proxy.provides)

    await runtime.disable(esphome)  # it holds on to it: it goes all the same
    assert proxy not in runtime.peripherals
    assert proxy.calls == ["start", "stop"]
    assert router.peripherals.endpoints("ble") == []

async def test_one_that_failed_stays_failed_when_brought_along_anew(tmp_path):

async def test_a_second_one_of_a_key_is_left_out_and_logged_once(tmp_path, caplog):
    first = FakePeripheral("mqtt", provides=[Endpoint("mqtt", "a", "x", is_shared=True)], is_on_demand=True)
    second = FakePeripheral("mqtt", provides=[Endpoint("mqtt", "b", "y", is_shared=True)], is_on_demand=True)
    one, two = FakePeripheral("one", [Need("mqtt", ["a"])]), FakePeripheral("two", [Need("mqtt", ["b"])])
    output = RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, first, one, second, two, output=output)
    await runtime.refresh()

    assert runtime.peripherals == [first, one, two] and runtime.peripheral("mqtt") is first
    with pytest.raises(LookupError):
        runtime.status(second)  # nothing the Hub keys by its key: no status, no settings, never gone
    assert output.last("mqtt") == PeripheralStatus(S.RUNNING) and second.calls == []
    assert (state(runtime, one), runtime.status(two)) == (
        S.RUNNING,
        PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, "need mqtt/b: nothing offers it"),
    )
    assert caplog.text.count("Another peripheral has the key mqtt") == 1

async def test_adding_one_whose_key_is_taken_raises(tmp_path):
    output, original = RecordingRuntimeOutput(), FakePeripheral("zigbee")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, original, output=output)
    fork = FakePeripheral("zigbee")  # e.g. a fork installed beside the original

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="another peripheral has the key zigbee"):
        await runtime.add(fork)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert runtime.peripherals == [original] and output.last("zigbee") == PeripheralStatus(S.RUNNING)
    await runtime.remove(fork)  # never added: nothing goes
    assert output.disappeared == [] and state(runtime, original) == S.RUNNING


async def test_what_uses_a_provider_stops_before_it(tmp_path):
    stopped: list[str] = []

    class Logged(FakePeripheral):
        async def stop(self):
            stopped.append(self.name)

    server = Logged("matter-server", provides=[SERVER], is_on_demand=True)

    await runtime.enable(app)
    await settle(runtime)
    stopped.clear()
    await runtime.stop()
    assert stopped == ["app", "bridge", "matter-server"]

# readiness


class Gated(FakePeripheral):
    """Serves once ``gate`` opens: its start returns then."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.gate = asyncio.Event()

    async def start(self):
        await super().start()
        await self.gate.wait()


async def test_what_needs_a_provider_starts_once_its_start_returned(tmp_path):
    server = Gated("matter-server", provides=[SERVER], is_on_demand=True)
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("matter")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, server, matter, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, server) == S.STARTING, settled=False)
    assert runtime.status(matter) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_STARTING, "waiting for matter-server")

    server.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert state(runtime, matter) == S.RUNNING


async def test_a_running_peripheral_rides_out_its_provider_restarting(tmp_path):
    server = Gated("matter-server", provides=[SERVER], is_on_demand=True)
    server.gate.set()
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("matter")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, server, matter)

    server.gate.clear()
    await runtime.restart(server)
    assert state(runtime, server) == S.STARTING
    assert state(runtime, matter) == S.RUNNING and matter.calls == ["start"]
    server.gate.set()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("ends", ["restart", "disable"])
async def test_what_runs_on_an_in_process_provider_stops_first_and_starts_once_it_runs_again(tmp_path, ends):
    order: list[str] = []

    class Ordered(Gated):
        async def start(self):
            order.append(f"{self.name} start")
            await super().start()

        async def stop(self):
            order.append(f"{self.name} stop")

    zeroconf, homekit = Ordered("zeroconf", is_on_demand=True), Ordered("homekit", [Need("mdns")])
    zeroconf.provided = [Endpoint("mdns", "zeroconf", "zeroconf", is_shared=True, instance=zeroconf)]  # its browser
    zeroconf.gate.set()
    homekit.gate.set()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, zeroconf, homekit)

    order.clear()
    zeroconf.gate.clear()
    await getattr(runtime, ends)(zeroconf)
    assert order[:2] == ["homekit stop", "zeroconf stop"]  # what it registered goes with the one that ran

    if ends == "disable":
        await runtime.enable(zeroconf)
    assert runtime.status(homekit) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_STARTING, "waiting for zeroconf")
    zeroconf.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert order[2:] == ["zeroconf start", "homekit start"] and state(runtime, homekit) == S.RUNNING


async def test_an_optional_need_is_handed_over_once_its_provider_runs(tmp_path):
    border = Gated("otbr", provides=[THREAD], is_on_demand=True)
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", is_required=False)], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, border, matter, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, matter) == S.RUNNING, settled=False)
    assert state(runtime, border) == S.STARTING  # it doesn't hold it back
    assert matter.peripherals.bound == {}  # nor is it handed over before it serves
    assert runtime.bound(matter) == runtime.providers(matter) == {}  # what the Hub shows: what it was handed

    border.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert matter.changes == [PeripheralChange("thread", None, THREAD)] and matter.calls == ["start"]
    assert (runtime.bound(matter), runtime.providers(matter)) == ({"thread": THREAD}, {"thread": "otbr"})


async def test_an_optional_need_rides_out_its_provider_restarting(tmp_path):
    border = Gated("otbr", provides=[THREAD], is_on_demand=True)
    border.gate.set()
    matter = FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", is_required=False)], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, border, matter)
    changes = list(matter.changes)

    border.gate.clear()
    await runtime.restart(border)
    assert state(runtime, border) == S.STARTING
    assert matter.peripherals.endpoint("thread") == THREAD and matter.changes == changes
    border.gate.set()


# a start cut short


async def starting(tmp_path, *peripherals: FakePeripheral):
    """A runtime of ``peripherals`` with the last one in the middle of its start, held there."""
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, *peripherals, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: peripherals[-1].calls == ["start"], settled=False)
    return runtime


async def test_a_start_cut_short_by_disabling_it_stays_disabled(tmp_path):
    slow = Gated("slow")
    runtime = await starting(tmp_path, slow)
    await runtime.disable(slow)
    slow.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert (state(runtime, slow), slow.calls) == (S.DISABLED, ["start", "stop"])


async def test_a_start_cut_short_by_a_restart_starts_anew(tmp_path):
    slow = Gated("slow")
    runtime = await starting(tmp_path, slow)
    await runtime.restart(slow)
    await until(runtime, lambda: slow.calls == ["start", "stop", "start"], settled=False)
    slow.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert (state(runtime, slow), slow.calls) == (S.RUNNING, ["start", "stop", "start"])


async def test_a_start_cut_short_by_losing_its_need_waits_for_it(tmp_path):
    stick, slow = radio(ZIGBEE), Gated("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")])
    runtime = await starting(tmp_path, stick, slow)
    stick.provided = []
    await changed(runtime, stick)
    assert runtime.status(slow) == PeripheralStatus(S.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, UNBOUND)
    assert slow.calls == ["start", "stop"]


async def test_a_start_cut_short_by_the_runtime_stopping_is_stopped(tmp_path):
    slow = Gated("slow")
    runtime = await starting(tmp_path, slow)
    await runtime.stop()
    assert slow.calls == ["start", "stop"]


async def test_one_replaced_by_another_of_its_name_goes_and_the_other_runs(tmp_path):
    output, old, new = RecordingRuntimeOutput(), FakePeripheral("aa"), FakePeripheral("aa")
    esphome = FakePeripheral("esphome", provides=[old])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, esphome, output=output)

    esphome.provided[:] = [new]  # the node reconnected
    await changed(runtime, esphome)
    assert (old.calls, output.disappeared) == (["start", "stop"], [old])
    assert state(runtime, new) == S.RUNNING and runtime.peripheral("esphome/aa") is new


# settings and platform facts


async def test_settings_are_kept_and_handed_over_or_restart_it(tmp_path):
    class Channel(BaseModel):
        channel: int = 11

    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel, answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)
    assert integration.settings == Channel()

    assert await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15}) == Channel(channel=15)
    assert integration.changes == [("settings", Channel())]
    assert integration.calls == ["start"]

    integration.answer = False
    await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 20})
    await settle(runtime)
    assert integration.calls == ["start", "stop", "start"]

    again = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    await run(tmp_path, again)  # the same data: after a reboot
    assert again.settings == Channel(channel=20)


async def test_one_without_settings_takes_none(tmp_path):

    assert host.settings == NoSettings()
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        await runtime.update_settings(host, {"x": 1})
    await runtime.update_settings(host, {})
    assert runtime.state["settings"] == {}  # nothing kept for it


async def test_changed_facts_replace_the_platform_and_are_handed_over_or_restart_it(tmp_path):
    handles, restarts = FakePeripheral("handles", answer=True), FakePeripheral("restarts")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, handles, restarts)
    before, europe = runtime.platform, replace(runtime.platform, region="Europe")

    await runtime.update_platform(europe)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert runtime.platform is handles.platform is restarts.platform is europe
    assert handles.changes == restarts.changes == [("platform", before)]
    assert (handles.calls, restarts.calls) == (["start"], ["start", "stop", "start"])


async def test_changed_facts_reach_one_still_starting_once_it_runs(tmp_path):
    gate = asyncio.Event()

    class Slow(FakePeripheral):
        async def start(self):
            await super().start()
            await gate.wait()

    handles, restarts = Slow("handles", answer=True), Slow("restarts")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, handles, restarts, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, handles) == state(runtime, restarts) == S.STARTING, settled=False)

    before = runtime.platform
    await runtime.update_platform(replace(before, region="Europe"))  # it may have read the one before
    await runtime.update_platform(replace(before, region="USA"))
    assert handles.changes == restarts.changes == [] and handles.platform.region == "USA"
    gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert handles.changes == restarts.changes == [("platform", before)]  # once, since what it read
    assert (handles.calls, restarts.calls) == (["start"], ["start", "stop", "start"])
    assert state(runtime, handles) == state(runtime, restarts) == S.RUNNING


async def test_new_settings_reach_one_still_starting_once_it_runs(tmp_path):
    handles, restarts = Gated("handles", answer=True, settings=Channel), Gated("restarts", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, handles, restarts, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, handles) == state(runtime, restarts) == S.STARTING, settled=False)

    for slow in (handles, restarts):
        await runtime.update_settings(slow, {"channel": 15})  # it may have read the ones before
        await runtime.update_settings(slow, {"channel": 20})
    assert handles.changes == restarts.changes == []
    handles.gate.set()
    restarts.gate.set()
    await settle(runtime)
    assert handles.changes == restarts.changes == [("settings", Channel())]  # once, since what it read
    assert (handles.calls, restarts.calls) == (["start"], ["start", "stop", "start"])
    assert handles.settings == restarts.settings == Channel(channel=20)
    assert state(runtime, handles) == state(runtime, restarts) == S.RUNNING


async def test_facts_that_restart_one_once_it_runs_leave_it_to_read_its_new_settings(tmp_path):
    restarts = Gated("restarts", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, restarts, settled=False)

    assert restarts.calls == ["start", "stop", "start"] and restarts.settings == Channel(channel=15)

async def test_any_peripheral_reads_the_facts_and_what_it_learned_replaces_the_platform(tmp_path):
    output, europe = RecordingRuntimeOutput(), Platform(documents_root=tmp_path, region="Europe")
    router, matter = FakePeripheral("my-border-router"), FakePeripheral("matter", answer=True)  # one of the user's own
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, router, matter, output=output, platform=europe)
    assert router.platform.region == "Europe"

    await router.output.peripheral_did_learn(router, {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})
    await settle(runtime)
    assert output.learned == [("my-border-router", {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})]  # for the host to keep
    assert matter.platform == runtime.platform == replace(europe, thread_dataset="0e08")
    assert matter.changes == [("platform", europe)]

    await router.output.peripheral_did_learn(router, {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})  # again, at the next boot
    await settle(runtime)
    assert matter.changes == [("platform", europe)]  # nothing changed


async def test_only_the_facts_a_platform_holds_are_learned(tmp_path):
    output, router = RecordingRuntimeOutput(), FakePeripheral("my-border-router")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, router, output=output)
    root = runtime.platform.documents_root

    learned = {"thread_dataset": "0e08", "thread_channel": 25, "documents_root": tmp_path / "elsewhere"}
    await router.output.peripheral_did_learn(router, learned)  # a newer peripheral's, and a resource: no facts
    await settle(runtime)
    assert output.learned == [("my-border-router", {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})]
    assert (runtime.platform.thread_dataset, runtime.platform.documents_root) == ("0e08", root)

    await router.output.peripheral_did_learn(router, {"thread_channel": 26})
    await settle(runtime)
    assert len(output.learned) == 1


async def test_one_added_while_it_runs_runs_and_one_removed_is_gone(tmp_path):
    output, hue = RecordingRuntimeOutput(), FakePeripheral("hue")
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakePeripheral("host"), output=output)

    await runtime.add(hue)  # installed while the hub runs
    await settle(runtime)
    assert state(runtime, hue) == S.RUNNING

    await runtime.remove(hue)
    assert hue.calls == ["start", "stop"] and hue not in runtime.peripherals
    assert output.disappeared == [hue]


# one that misbehaves stops nothing else


class Channel(BaseModel):
    channel: int = 11


async def test_invalid_stored_settings_fail_only_their_peripheral(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps({"settings": {"zigbee": {"channel": "eleven"}}}))
    host, integration = FakePeripheral("host"), FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, host, integration)
    assert state(runtime, host) == S.RUNNING
    assert runtime.status(integration) == PeripheralStatus(
        S.FAILED,
        K.INVALID_SETTINGS,
        "Invalid settings: channel: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer",
    )
    assert runtime.stored_settings(integration) == {"channel": "eleven"}  # what the Hub shows with the failure

    await runtime.restart(integration)  # the user tries again: they still don't validate
    await settle(runtime)
    assert runtime.status(integration).kind == K.INVALID_SETTINGS and integration.calls == []

    await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15})
    await settle(runtime)
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING and integration.settings == Channel(channel=15)
    assert runtime.stored_settings(integration) == {"channel": 15}


async def test_one_disabled_with_invalid_stored_settings_fails_once_enabled(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps({"settings": {"zigbee": {"channel": "eleven"}}}))
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration, disabled=MemoryDisabledStore(["zigbee"]))
    assert state(runtime, integration) == S.DISABLED

    await runtime.enable(integration)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert runtime.status(integration).kind == K.INVALID_SETTINGS and integration.calls == []


async def test_why_stored_settings_are_invalid_reads_as_they_load_also_while_disabled(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    stored = {"zigbee": {"channel": "eleven"}, "network": {"channel": "eleven", "permit_join": True}}
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps({"settings": stored}))
    integration, network = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel), FakePeripheral("network", settings=Network)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration, network, disabled=MemoryDisabledStore(["zigbee"]))

    error = runtime.settings_error(integration)  # what the Hub shows with them: it fails once enabled
    assert error is not None and [e["loc"] for e in error.errors()] == [("channel",)]
    assert runtime.settings_error(network) is None  # a read-only value is never loaded

    await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15})
    assert runtime.settings_error(integration) is None


async def test_stored_settings_it_no_longer_has_are_dropped(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    stored = {"zigbee": {"channel": 15, "pan_id": 1}, "host": {"old": 1}}  # the host's update dropped its settings
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps({"settings": stored}))
    host, integration = FakePeripheral("host"), FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, host, integration)

    assert state(runtime, host) == state(runtime, integration) == S.RUNNING
    assert integration.settings == Channel(channel=15)
    assert json.loads((tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").read_text())["settings"] == {"zigbee": {"channel": 15}}


async def test_new_settings_it_doesnt_have_are_refused(tmp_path):
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="pan_id"):
        await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15, "pan_id": 1})
    assert integration.settings == Channel() and runtime.state["settings"] == {"zigbee": {"channel": 11}}


class Network(BaseModel):
    channel: int = Field(
        11, json_schema_extra={Extra.read_only: True}
    )  # the live network's, filled in by the peripheral
    permit_join: bool = False


async def test_a_read_only_setting_is_filled_in_by_its_peripheral_and_never_changed_by_an_update(tmp_path):
    assert Network.model_json_schema()["properties"]["channel"]["readOnly"] is True
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Network, answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)
    integration.settings.channel = 25  # the network it found

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="frozen"):
        await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15})
    assert integration.settings == Network(channel=25) and integration.changes == []

    assert await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 25, "permit_join": True}) == Network(
        channel=25, permit_join=True
    )
    assert integration.changes == [("settings", Network(channel=25))]


async def test_a_read_only_setting_is_never_kept(tmp_path):
    """It shows what the peripheral filled in while it runs, never a value kept from before (the user's, when the field
    wasn't read-only yet)."""
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps({"settings": {"zigbee": {"channel": 15}}}))
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Network)
    runtime = Runtime(tmp_path / "data", [integration], platform=build_test_platform(tmp_path))
    assert integration.settings == Network() and runtime.state["settings"] == {"zigbee": {"permit_join": False}}

    await runtime.start()
    integration.settings.channel = 25
    await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"permit_join": True})
    assert json.loads((tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").read_text())["settings"] == {"zigbee": {"permit_join": True}}
    await runtime.stop()


class Keys(BaseModel):
    network_key: str = Field("", json_schema_extra={Extra.write_only: True})  # set by the user, never shown
    region: str = "Europe"


async def test_a_write_only_setting_is_kept_when_an_update_leaves_it_out(tmp_path):
    """The host never shows it, so an update of the others comes without it: the one kept stays."""
    assert Keys.model_json_schema()["properties"]["network_key"]["writeOnly"] is True
    server = FakePeripheral("zwave-js-server", settings=Keys)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, server)
    await runtime.update_settings(server, {"network_key": "secret"})

    assert await runtime.update_settings(server, {"region": "USA"}) == Keys(network_key="secret", region="USA")
    assert runtime.stored_settings(server) == {"network_key": "secret", "region": "USA"}  # kept, unlike a read-only one

async def test_a_corrupt_state_starts_afresh(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "data").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").write_text('{"settings": {"zigbee": {"chan')  # cut by a crash
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)

async def test_the_state_is_written_whole_or_not_at_all(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    integration = FakePeripheral("zigbee", settings=Channel)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, integration)
    await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 15})
    kept = (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").read_text()

    def crash(self, text: str):
        open(self, "w").close()  # the file is cut, then the power goes
        raise OSError("power lost")

    monkeypatch.setattr(type(tmp_path), "write_text", crash)
    with pytest.raises(OSError):
        await runtime.update_settings(integration, {"channel": 20})
    assert (tmp_path / "data" / "state.json").read_text() == kept

"""Containers as peripherals: what they render, the ports they get, when they are ready, what they learn."""

import asyncio
import json
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest
import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel
from support import changed, run, settle, state, until

from majordom_integration_sdk import Endpoint, Need, Platform, Service
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import PeripheralState, PeripheralStatus
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime import StatusKind as K
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose import Compose
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeCompose, FakePeripheral, RecordingRuntimeOutput

IP = Endpoint("ip", is_shared=True)
MULTIPAN = Endpoint("multipan", "silabs-cpc", "/dev/ttyUSB0", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})
NCP = Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "/dev/ttyUSB1", params={"baud": 115200, "flow_control": True})
RCP = Endpoint("thread", "spinel", "/dev/ttyUSB2", params={"baud": 460800, "flow_control": True})


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def listening(monkeypatch) -> set[int]:
    """Host ports something listens on; none unless a test says so."""
    ports: set[int] = set()
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose._is_listening", ports.__contains__
    )
    return ports


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def no_thread_network(monkeypatch):
    """The built-in border routers form and read no real network."""

    async def nothing(*args: Any):
        return None

    for talking in ("join_network", "active_dataset", "network_channel", "move_channel"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(builtin, talking, nothing)


def host() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("host", provides=[IP])


def stick(name: str, *provides: Endpoint) -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral(name, provides=provides)


def zigbee() -> FakePeripheral:
    return FakePeripheral("zigbee", [Need("zigbee")])


def matter(**compose: Any) -> tuple[FakePeripheral, Service]:
    server = Service(
        "matterjs-server",
        compose={"image": "matter", "environment": {"OTBR": "{peripherals.thread.url}"} | compose},
        needs=[Need("ip"), Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"], is_required=False)],
        provides=[Endpoint("matter", "matter-server-ws", "ws://127.0.0.1:{ports.api}/ws")],
        ports={"api": 5580},
    )
    return FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("matter", ["matter-server-ws"])]), server


def compose(tmp_path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return json.loads((tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals" / "compose" / "compose.json").read_text())["services"]


async def test_a_multipan_stick_serves_zigbee_and_matter_through_one_container(tmp_path):
    radio, integration, (app, server), otbr = stick("sky", MULTIPAN), zigbee(), matter(), builtin.otbr()
    peripherals = (host(), radio, builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), otbr, integration, server, app)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)

    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == Endpoint("zigbee", "ezsp", "socket://127.0.0.1:9999")
    assert app.peripherals.endpoint("matter").url == "ws://127.0.0.1:5580/ws"
    services = compose(tmp_path)
    assert set(services) == {"silabs-multiprotocol", "matterjs-server"}  # no one binds the standalone border router
    assert services["silabs-multiprotocol"]["devices"][0] == "/dev/ttyUSB0:/dev/ttyRCP"
    environment = services["silabs-multiprotocol"]["environment"]
    assert (environment["RADIO_BAUD"], environment["RADIO_FLOW_CONTROL"]) == ("460800", "True")
    assert services["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["OTBR"] == "http://127.0.0.1:8081"
    assert "depends_on" not in services["matterjs-server"]  # its border router coming and going doesn't restart it
    assert runtime.users(radio) == ["silabs-multiprotocol", "zigbee", "matterjs-server", "matter"]
    assert runtime.uses(app) == ["matterjs-server", "host", "silabs-multiprotocol", "compose", "sky"]
    assert runtime.reach([MULTIPAN]) == ["thread", "zigbee"]  # through the containers it would run
    assert runtime.status(otbr) == PeripheralStatus(
        PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_UNBOUND, "need thread/spinel: nothing offers it"
    )


async def test_learning_the_thread_network_recreates_no_border_router(tmp_path):
    containers = FakeCompose()
    network = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", thread_dataset="0e08hub")
    peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), zigbee())
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, *peripherals, platform=network)
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(network, thread_dataset="0e08learned"))  # provisioned onto it instead
    await settle(runtime)
    assert containers.calls[applied:] == []


async def test_split_radios_use_direct_zigbee_and_a_standalone_border_router(tmp_path):
    ncp, rcp, integration, (app, server) = stick("ncp", NCP), stick("rcp", RCP), zigbee(), matter()
    peripherals = (host(), ncp, rcp, builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), builtin.otbr(), integration, server, app)
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)

    assert integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee") == NCP
    assert set(compose(tmp_path)) == {"otbr", "matterjs-server"}
    assert compose(tmp_path)["otbr"]["devices"][0] == "/dev/ttyUSB2:/dev/ttyRCP"
    rcp_url = "spinel+hdlc+uart:///dev/ttyRCP?uart-baudrate=460800&uart-flow-control"
    assert compose(tmp_path)["otbr"]["environment"]["OT_RCP_DEVICE"] == rcp_url


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("router", "radio", "listening"),
    [(builtin.silabs_multiprotocol, MULTIPAN, "LISTEN_ADDRESS"), (builtin.otbr, RCP, "OT_REST_LISTEN_ADDR")],
)
async def test_a_border_router_answers_only_the_hub_unless_the_host_listens_on_the_lan(
    tmp_path, router, radio, listening
):
    service, matter = router(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), stick("radio", radio), service, matter)
    assert compose(tmp_path)[service.name]["environment"][listening] == "127.0.0.1"  # over loopback, on the host

    lab, service, matter = tmp_path / "lab", router(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    containers = FakeCompose(listen_address="0.0.0.0")  # a lab harness: no password guards it
    await run(lab, containers, host(), stick("radio", radio), service, matter)
    assert compose(lab)[service.name]["environment"][listening] == "0.0.0.0"
    assert "is_exposed_on_lan" not in service.Settings.model_fields  # the host's switch, not the user's


def test_the_harness_runs_matterjs_server_on_loopback_without_logging_the_thread_key():

    environment = harness["services"]["matterjs-server"]["environment"]

async def test_the_folders_a_container_binds_from_its_data_are_created_before_docker_would_as_root(tmp_path):

async def test_a_wipe_empties_a_service_s_data_through_docker_in_its_own_image(tmp_path):
    # its container wrote there as root, which the hub's user can't remove (a factory reset): the Thread network
    containers, otbr, matter = FakeCompose(), builtin.otbr(), FakePeripheral("matter", [Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"])])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), stick("rcp", RCP), otbr, matter)
    data = otbr.platform.documents_folder(otbr)
    (data / "0_a5c.data").write_text("dataset")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="runs"):
        await containers.wipe(otbr)  # its container would write on

    await runtime.stop()
    applied = len(containers.calls)
    await containers.wipe(otbr)
    assert containers.calls[applied:] == [
        ("run", "--rm", "--pull", "never", "--network", "none", "--userns", "host", "--user", "0", "--entrypoint")
        + ("find", "-v", f"{data}:/d", otbr.compose["image"], "/d", "-mindepth", "1", "-delete")
    ]

    (data / "0_a5c.data").unlink()
    await containers.wipe(otbr)
    assert len(containers.calls) == applied + 1  # nothing to remove: no container run

class Keys(BaseModel):
    key: str = "secret"


async def test_a_service_setting_recreates_only_that_service(tmp_path):
    zwave_server = Service(
        "zwave-js-server",
        compose={"image": "zwave", "environment": {"KEY": "{settings.key}"}},
        needs=[Need("ip")],
        provides=[Endpoint("zwave", "zwave-js-ws", "ws://127.0.0.1:3000")],
        settings=Keys,
    )
    zwave = FakePeripheral("zwave", [Need("zwave")])
    app, server = matter()
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), zwave_server, zwave, server, app)
    before = compose(tmp_path)
    assert before["zwave-js-server"]["environment"]["KEY"] == "secret"

    await runtime.update_settings(zwave_server, {"key": "other"})
    await settle(runtime)
    after = compose(tmp_path)
    assert {name for name in before if before[name] != after[name]} == {"zwave-js-server"}
    assert zwave.calls == ["start"]  # what it is bound to is the same: it reconnects on its own

async def test_a_moved_need_recreates_a_service_only_when_it_renders_otherwise(tmp_path):
    containers, radio = FakeCompose(), stick("sky", NCP)
    bridge = Service("bridge", {"devices": ["{peripherals.zigbee.url}:/dev/ttyRCP"]}, [Need("zigbee")], [Endpoint("b")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, radio, bridge, FakePeripheral("user", [Need("b")]))
    applied = len(containers.calls)

    radio.provided = [replace(NCP, params={"baud": 57600})]  # moved, but what it renders is the same

    radio.provided = [replace(NCP, url="/dev/ttyUSB9")]

async def test_the_platform_facts_render_and_a_change_recreates_only_what_renders_them(tmp_path):
    before, containers = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", region="Europe"), FakeCompose()
    app, server = matter(REGION="{platform.region}")
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("plain")], answer=True)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, containers, host(), server, app, plain, user, platform=before)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "Europe"

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(before, region="USA"))
    await settle(runtime)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["matterjs-server"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "USA"
    assert len([call for call in containers.calls[applied:] if "-f" in call]) == 2  # without it, then with it again
    assert runtime.status(server).state == PeripheralState.RUNNING
    assert app.changes == user.changes == [("platform", before)]  # the integrations hear it too


async def test_a_service_renders_only_when_it_is_created(tmp_path):
    class InPlace(Service):
        async def platform_facts_did_change(self, before: Platform) -> bool:
            return True  # it takes the region over its API

    europe = Platform(documents_root=tmp_path / "data" / "peripherals", region="Europe")
    radio = InPlace(
        "radio", {"image": "radio", "environment": {"REGION": "{platform.region}"}}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("r")]
    )
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("r"), Need("plain")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), radio, plain, user, platform=europe)

    await runtime.update_platform(replace(europe, region="USA"))
    await runtime.restart(plain)
    await settle(runtime)
    assert compose(tmp_path)["radio"]["environment"]["REGION"] == "Europe"  # not recreated behind its back


async def test_a_container_still_starting_is_recreated_once_it_serves_only_if_the_facts_render_it(tmp_path):

async def test_services_get_free_host_ports_and_keep_them(tmp_path, listening):
    async def ezsp() -> tuple[str, str]:
        """The zigbee URL bound after a (re)boot, and the port the container got."""
        integration = zigbee()
        peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), integration)
        runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), *peripherals)
        port = compose(tmp_path)["silabs-multiprotocol"]["environment"]["EZSP_TCP_PORT"]
        await runtime.stop()
        return integration.peripherals.endpoint("zigbee").url, port

    assert await ezsp() == ("socket://127.0.0.1:9999", "9999")  # the preferred port, free

    listening.add(9999)  # after a reboot something else took it before our container came up
    moved, port = await ezsp()
    assert moved == f"socket://127.0.0.1:{port}" != "socket://127.0.0.1:9999"

    listening.clear()  # the preferred port is free again: the service stays where it is now
    assert (await ezsp())[0] == moved


async def test_a_port_held_by_our_own_running_container_is_kept(tmp_path, listening, monkeypatch):

async def test_services_preferring_the_same_port_get_different_ones(tmp_path):
    bridge = Service(
        "bridge",

class Router(Service):
    """A border router that is set up once it answers and knows its Thread network."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("router", {"image": "router"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("thread", "rest", "http://ours")])
        self.release, self.calls = asyncio.Event(), []

    async def provision(self, endpoint: Endpoint):
        await self.release.wait()
        self.calls.append(("provision", endpoint.url))

    async def start(self):
        await super().start()
        self.calls.append(("learn", "http://ours"))
        await self.output.peripheral_did_learn(self, {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})


async def test_what_needs_a_service_waits_for_its_setup_then_hears_what_it_learned(tmp_path):
    router, output = Router(), RecordingRuntimeOutput()
    thread = FakePeripheral("thread", [Need("thread")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, FakeCompose(), host(), router, thread, output=output, settled=False)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, router) == PeripheralState.STARTING, settled=False)
    assert runtime.status(thread) == PeripheralStatus(PeripheralState.WAITING, K.NEEDS_STARTING, "waiting for router")

    await runtime.refresh()  # something else changed meanwhile: its setup goes on
    router.release.set()
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, thread) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert router.calls == [("provision", "http://ours"), ("learn", "http://ours")]
    assert output.learned == [("router", {"thread_dataset": "0e08"})]

    await runtime.restart(router)  # recreated: it may hold another network now
    await until(runtime, lambda: len(output.learned) == 2)
    assert router.calls[-2:] == [("provision", "http://ours"), ("learn", "http://ours")]
    assert thread.calls == ["start"]


class Docker:
    """Docker, faked: ``calls`` it got; a container runs once applied, and its ports answer while ``is_answering``.
    Applying fails while ``failure`` is set; it isn't reachable unless ``is_reachable``, can't tell what runs unless
    ``is_listing``."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []
        self.applied: list[set[str]] = []  # the services of each compose file it took
        self.composes: list[Compose] = []
        self.is_answering = self.is_reachable = self.is_listing = True
        self.left_running: set[str] = set()  # containers that outlived the runtime that ran them
        self.failure = b""
        self.gate: asyncio.Event | None = None  # while set, applying waits for it

    async def exec(self, *args: str, **kwargs: Any) -> "Process":
        self.calls.append(args)
        if "info" in args:
            return Process(b"", 0 if self.is_reachable else 1)
        if "ps" in args:
            running = "\n".join({*self.left_running, *(name for c in self.composes for name in c._running)})
            return Process(running.encode(), 0 if self.is_listing else 1)
        self.applied.append(set(json.loads(Path(args[args.index("-f") + 1]).read_text())["services"]))
        return Process(self.failure, 1 if self.failure else 0, self.gate)

    def holds(self, port: int) -> bool:
        running = (
            ports for compose in self.composes for name, ports in compose.ports.items() if name in compose._running
        )
        return self.is_answering and any(port in ports.values() for ports in running)


class Process:
    def __init__(self, output: bytes, returncode: int, gate: asyncio.Event | None = None):
        self.output, self.returncode, self.gate = output, returncode, gate

    async def communicate(self) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
        if self.gate:
            await self.gate.wait()
        return self.output, b""


@pytest.fixture
def docker(monkeypatch, listening) -> Docker:
    docker, init = Docker(), Compose.__init__

    def record(self):
        init(self)
        docker.composes.append(self)

    monkeypatch.setattr(Compose, "__init__", record)
    monkeypatch.setattr("asyncio.create_subprocess_exec", docker.exec)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services.compose._is_listening",
        lambda port: port in listening or docker.holds(port),
    )
    return docker

async def test_restarting_a_service_recreates_only_its_container(tmp_path, docker):
    app, server = matter()
    integration = zigbee()
    peripherals = (host(), stick("sky", MULTIPAN), builtin.silabs_multiprotocol(), integration, server, app)
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), *peripherals)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == state(runtime, integration) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    before = compose(tmp_path)

    await runtime.restart(server)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, server) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)
    assert compose(tmp_path) == before
    assert [call[-1] for call in docker.calls if "-f" in call][-2:] == ["--remove-orphans"] * 2  # without, with it
    assert (app.calls, integration.calls) == (["start"], ["start"])


async def test_a_container_whose_start_was_stopped_is_taken_down(tmp_path, docker):
    app, server = matter()
    plain = Service("plain", {"image": "plain"}, [Need("ip")], [Endpoint("plain")])
    user = FakePeripheral("user", [Need("plain")])
    runtime = await run(tmp_path, Compose(), host(), server, app)
    await until(runtime, lambda: state(runtime, app) == PeripheralState.RUNNING)

    docker.gate = asyncio.Event()
    runtime.given += [plain, user]
    refresh = asyncio.ensure_future(runtime.refresh())
    await until(runtime, lambda: docker.applied[-1] == {"matterjs-server", "plain"}, settled=False)
    asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(0.05, docker.gate.set)  # docker takes it after all
    await runtime.disable(user)
    await refresh
    await settle(runtime)
    assert docker.applied[-1] == {"matterjs-server"}

def dataset(network: str, channel: int = 15) -> str:
    """An active dataset's hex TLVs: its timestamp, channel and Extended PAN ID (the network)."""
    return f"0e080000000000010000000300{channel:04x}0208{network}"


HUB, OTHER = dataset("dead00beef00cafe"), dataset("0123456789abcdef")
ENABLE, DISABLE = ("/node/state", json.dumps("enable")), ("/node/state", json.dumps("disable"))
PENDING = "/node/dataset/pending"


def rest(url: str) -> Endpoint:
    return Endpoint("thread", "otbr-rest", url, is_shared=True)


@pytest.fixture
def border_router():
    """A border router's REST API with no network until one is put, and no change of it pending: one put lands at
    once, one pending while ``landing`` lands right after its active dataset is read. It refuses puts to the path
    ``refused`` names, and fails each put in ``failing`` once."""
    state: dict[str, Any] = {"dataset": "", "pending": "", "thread": "leader", "puts": [], "failing": []}

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_GET(self):
            read = {PENDING: state["pending"], "/node/state": json.dumps(state["thread"])}
            body = read.get(self.path, state["dataset"]).encode()
            self.send_response(200 if body else 204)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)
            if self.path == "/node/dataset/active" and state.get("landing"):
                state["dataset"], state["pending"], state["landing"] = state["pending"], "", False

        def do_PUT(self):
            body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])).decode()
            state["puts"].append((self.path, body))
            if self.path == state.get("refused") or (self.path, body) in state["failing"]:
                with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
                    state["failing"].remove((self.path, body))
                self.send_response(409)
                self.end_headers()
                return
            if self.path == "/node/state":
                state["thread"] = "disabled" if body == json.dumps("disable") else "leader"
            if self.path == "/node/dataset/active" and not state.get("stuck"):
                state["dataset"] = body if body.startswith("0e") else "0e08newnetwork"
            elif self.path == PENDING:
                state["dataset"] = body  # its delay passed
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()

        def log_message(self, format, *args):
            pass

    server = ThreadingTCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)  # HTTPServer would resolve the host name first
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, args=(0.01,), daemon=True).start()
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}", state
    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()

def test_a_move_is_stamped_after_the_network_it_moves_with_the_clock_behind(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(services.time, "time", lambda: 1000)  # a Pi without a clock of its own, before NTP
    stamped = (2_000_000_000 << 16).to_bytes(8).hex()  # by an earlier move, with the clock right
    moved = services._tlvs(services._moved(f"0e08{stamped}000300000f0208dead00beef00cafe", 20))
    assert int.from_bytes(moved[services._ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP]) >> 16 == 2_000_000_001  # newer: the devices take it
    assert moved[services._PENDING_TIMESTAMP] == moved[services._ACTIVE_TIMESTAMP]

class Answering:
    """Runs nothing: the border router at ``url`` answers already, and is set up as the runtime's containers are."""

    def __init__(self, url: str):
        self.url = url

    def provided(self, service: Service) -> list[Endpoint]:
        return [replace(endpoint, url=self.url) for endpoint in service.templates]

    async def up(self, service: Service):
        for endpoint in service.provides:
            await service.provision(endpoint)

    async def down(self, service: Service):
        pass

    def is_current(self, service: Service) -> bool:
        return True


def serving[S: Service](service: S, url: str, **facts: Any) -> S:
    """``service`` on the border router at ``url``, the platform holding ``facts``; what it tells recorded."""
    service.platform = build_test_platform(**facts)
    service.peripherals = Peripherals({"container": Endpoint("container", "compose", instance=Answering(url))})
    service.output = RecordingPeripheralOutput()
    return service


def learned(service: Service) -> list[tuple[Peripheral, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
    return cast(RecordingPeripheralOutput, service.output).learned


@pytest.mark.parametrize("router", [otbr, silabs_multiprotocol])
async def test_a_border_router_tells_its_thread_network_once_it_serves(border_router, router):
    url, state = border_router
    state["dataset"] = dataset("0123456789abcdef")
    service = serving(router(), url)
    await asyncio.wait_for(service.start(), 3)
    assert learned(service) == [(service, {"thread_dataset": dataset("0123456789abcdef")})]

# FILE: tests/runtime/test_thread_source.py
================================================================================
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.services import builtin as services

SCRIPT = services._IMAGES / "thread-source" / "run"

# A stand-in for iproute2: answers the queries the script makes from a JSON state and applies its route changes.
FAKE_IP = f"""#!{sys.executable}
import ipaddress, json, sys
from pathlib import Path

state_file = Path(__file__).with_name("state.json")
state = json.loads(state_file.read_text())
args = sys.argv[1:]
if args[:5] == ["-o", "-6", "addr", "show", "dev"]:
    if args[5] not in state["addr"]:
        sys.exit(f'Device "{{args[5]}}" does not exist.')
    print("\\n".join(state["addr"][args[5]]))
elif args[:4] == ["-6", "route", "show", "match"]:
    address = ipaddress.ip_address(args[4])
    for dst, line in state["routes"].get(args[6], {{}}).items():
        if dst != "default" and address in ipaddress.ip_network(dst):
            print(f"{{dst}} {{line}}")
elif args[:3] == ["-6", "route", "replace"]:
    state["replaced"].append(args[3:])
    state["routes"][args[5]][args[3]] = " ".join(args[6:])
    state_file.write_text(json.dumps(state))
else:
    sys.exit(f"unexpected: ip {{' '.join(args)}}")
"""

ETH0 = [
    "2: eth0    inet6 fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:ce47:229:37f5:dc98/64 scope global temporary dynamic",
    "2: eth0    inet6 2a0a:a548:cced:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d/64 scope global dynamic mngtmpaddr proto kernel_ra",
    "2: eth0    inet6 fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d/64 scope global dynamic mngtmpaddr proto kernel_ra",
]
WPAN0 = [
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111:0:ff:fe00:fc11/64 scope global nodad deprecated",
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd11:ec6a:d233:1:5465:34b9:c5b4:2b7c/64 scope global nodad",
    "7: wpan0    inet6 fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111:f746:74ed:1eb7:e84/64 scope global nodad deprecated",
]
OMR, MESH_LOCAL = "fd11:ec6a:d233:1::/64", "fd4c:60e5:af3f:4111::/64"
STABLE_ULA = "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:8aa2:9eff:fea7:d66d"
KERNEL_ROUTE = "proto kernel metric 256 pref medium"


@pytest.fixture
def host(tmp_path: Path):
    """The border router's host as `ip` shows it: Thread routes as the kernel adds them for wpan0's addresses."""
    (tmp_path / "ip").write_text(FAKE_IP)
    (tmp_path / "ip").chmod(0o755)
    state = {
        "addr": {"eth0": ETH0, "wpan0": WPAN0},
        "routes": {"wpan0": {OMR: KERNEL_ROUTE, MESH_LOCAL: KERNEL_ROUTE}},
        "replaced": [],
    }
    (tmp_path / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state))
    return tmp_path


def sync(host: Path) -> dict:
    env = {"PATH": f"{host}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}", "OT_THREAD_IF": "wpan0", "BACKBONE_IF": "eth0"}
    subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", f'source "{SCRIPT}" && sync_sources'], env=env, check=True, timeout=10)
    return json.loads((host / "state.json").read_text())


def edit(host: Path, change):
    state = json.loads((host / "state.json").read_text())
    change(state)
    (host / "state.json").write_text(json.dumps(state))


def test_routes_to_the_border_routers_own_thread_addresses_take_a_stable_backbone_ula(host):
    state = sync(host)
    assert state["replaced"] == [[OMR, "dev", "wpan0", *KERNEL_ROUTE.split(), "src", STABLE_ULA]]
    assert MESH_LOCAL not in {r[0] for r in state["replaced"]}  # only deprecated addresses of ours there


def test_a_route_with_the_source_already_is_left_alone(host):
    sync(host)
    assert len(sync(host)["replaced"]) == 1


def test_follows_the_border_router_re_adding_its_route(host):
    sync(host)
    edit(host, lambda s: s["routes"]["wpan0"].update({OMR: KERNEL_ROUTE}))
    assert len(sync(host)["replaced"]) == 2


def test_follows_the_backbone_renumbering(host):
    sync(host)
    renumbered = "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:1111:2222:3333:4444"
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=[ETH0[2].replace(STABLE_ULA, renumbered)]))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"][-1][-2:] == ["src", renumbered]


def test_a_temporary_ula_when_there_is_no_stable_one(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=ETH0[:2]))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"][0][-1] == "fdc0:ca84:d7e3:0:ce47:229:37f5:dc98"


def test_without_a_backbone_ula_nothing_changes(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].update(eth0=[ETH0[1]]))  # a GUA: nodes may have no route back to it
    assert sync(host)["replaced"] == []


def test_without_a_thread_interface_nothing_changes(host):
    edit(host, lambda s: s["addr"].pop("wpan0"))
    assert sync(host)["replaced"] == []


def test_both_border_routers_run_it():
    assert f"{SCRIPT.parent}:/etc/services.d/thread-source:ro" in services.otbr().compose["volumes"]  # s6 starts it
    assert f"{SCRIPT}:/thread-source:ro" in services.silabs_multiprotocol().compose["volumes"]
    assert "bash /thread-source &" in (services._IMAGES / "multiprotocol" / "entrypoint.sh").read_text()

"""The runtime's DNS-SD browser, over fakes of zeroconf's: no multicast socket is opened."""

from typing import cast

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers import zeroconf as module
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.zeroconf import ZeroconfDiscoveryService


class Browser:
    def __init__(self, zeroconf: object, services: list[str], listener: object):
        self.cancels = 0

    async def async_cancel(self):
        self.cancels += 1


class AsyncZeroconf:
    zeroconf = None

    async def async_close(self):
        pass


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def fakes(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "AsyncZeroconf", AsyncZeroconf)
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "AsyncServiceBrowser", Browser)


async def test_a_registration_cancelled_after_it_stopped_is_gone_already():
    zeroconf = ZeroconfDiscoveryService()
    await zeroconf.start()
    cancel = zeroconf.register(object(), {"_esphomelib._tcp.local."})
    [browser] = cast(set[Browser], zeroconf._browsers)
    await zeroconf.stop()  # before a user that cancels only then

    cancel()
    assert browser.cancels == 1 and zeroconf._adapters == []

"""Secure channels: credentials are written to a BLE device only over a link secured first (LE Secure Connections),
through a radio that can pair, or over an unsecured one only when asked for by name."""

import logging
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock

import pytest

from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import (
    BLEConnection,
    BLEPairingError,
    LESecureConnections,
    PairableBLEConnection,
    Unsecured,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.router import BLEService
from majordom_integration_sdk.testing import FakeBLESource


def pairable(calls: list[str] | None = None) -> Mock:
    connection = Mock(spec=PairableBLEConnection)
    connection.pair = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda: calls.append("pair") if calls is not None else None)
    connection.unpair = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda: calls.append("unpair") if calls is not None else None)
    connection.write = AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda *_, **__: calls.append("write") if calls is not None else None)
    return connection


async def test_le_secure_connections_pairs_before_any_write_and_unpairs_after():
    calls: list[str] = []
    connection = pairable(calls)

    async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection) as secured:
        await secured.write(1, b"secret")

    assert calls == ["pair", "write", "unpair"]


async def test_le_secure_connections_refuses_a_connection_that_cannot_pair():
    connection = Mock(spec=BLEConnection)

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="can't pair"):
        async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection):
            pytest.fail("credentials would cross an unencrypted link")
    connection.write.assert_not_called()


async def test_a_failed_pairing_yields_nothing():
    connection = pairable()
    connection.pair.side_effect = BLEPairingError("authentication failed")

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError):
        async with LESecureConnections().secure(connection):
            pytest.fail("credentials would cross an unencrypted link")
    connection.write.assert_not_called()


async def test_the_bond_is_kept_when_asked():
    connection = pairable()

    async with LESecureConnections(is_pairing_kept=True).secure(connection):
        pass

    connection.unpair.assert_not_called()


async def test_unsecured_writes_as_is_and_says_so(caplog):
    connection = Mock(spec=BLEConnection)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
        async with Unsecured().secure(connection) as secured:
            assert secured is connection
    assert "unencrypted" in caplog.text
    assert not Unsecured.is_pairing_needed and LESecureConnections.is_pairing_needed


@pytest.fixture
async def radios():
    proxy = FakeBLESource("proxy", connection=Mock(spec=BLEConnection))  # stronger, can't pair
    adapter = FakeBLESource("adapter", connection=pairable(), is_pairable=True)
    ble = BLEService(sources=[proxy, adapter])
    await ble.start()
    proxy.advertise("AA", rssi=-40)
    adapter.advertise("AA", rssi=-70)
    yield ble, proxy, adapter
    await ble.stop()


async def test_a_pairing_lease_takes_a_radio_that_can_pair_over_a_stronger_one(radios):
    ble, proxy, adapter = radios

    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test", is_pairing_needed=True) as lease:
        assert lease.source == "adapter"
    async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test") as lease:
        assert lease.source == "proxy"


async def test_a_pairing_lease_fails_when_no_radio_hearing_the_device_can_pair(radios):
    ble, proxy, adapter = radios
    adapter.is_pairable = False

    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="can pair"):
        async with ble.exclusive("AA", owner="test", is_pairing_needed=True, timeout=0.1):
            pytest.fail("leased a radio that can't pair")


@pytest.fixture

    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module

async def test_on_linux_a_local_adapter_pairs_through_its_own_bluez_agent(adapter_client, monkeypatch):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    monkeypatch.setattr(module.sys, "platform", "linux")
    paired = AsyncMock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "pair_through_agent", paired)
    adapter = LocalAdapter("hci1")
    assert adapter.is_pairable

    connection = await adapter.connect("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", lambda: None)
    assert isinstance(connection, PairableBLEConnection)
    await connection.pair()
    paired.assert_awaited_once_with("hci1", "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF")
    adapter_client.pair.assert_not_called()  # bleak's brings no agent: Secure Connections fails without one
    await connection.unpair()
    adapter_client.unpair.assert_awaited_once()

    paired.side_effect = ConnectionError("org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed: Authentication Failed")
    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="AuthenticationFailed"):
        await connection.pair()


async def test_elsewhere_the_os_pairs_on_its_own(adapter_client, monkeypatch):
    from bleak.exc import BleakError

    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as module
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble.bluez import LocalAdapter

    monkeypatch.setattr(module.sys, "platform", "darwin")
    connection = await LocalAdapter().connect("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", lambda: None)
    assert isinstance(connection, PairableBLEConnection)

    await connection.pair()
    adapter_client.pair.assert_awaited_once()
    adapter_client.pair.side_effect = BleakError("refused")
    with pytest.raises(BLEPairingError, match="refused"):
        await connection.pair()


DEVICE = "/org/bluez/hci0/dev_AA_BB_CC_DD_EE_FF"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("member", "body", "answer"),
    [
        ("RequestAuthorization", [DEVICE], ("", [])),  # Just Works on LE Secure Connections
        ("RequestConfirmation", [DEVICE, 1234], ("", [])),
        ("RequestPasskey", [DEVICE], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("RequestAuthorization", ["/org/bluez/hci0/dev_11_22_33_44_55_66"], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("RequestPinCode", [DEVICE], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("AuthorizeService", [DEVICE, "0000110b-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"], "org.bluez.Error.Rejected"),
        ("Release", [], ("", [])),
    ],
)
def test_the_agent_answers_only_for_the_device_being_paired(member, body, answer):
    from majordom_integration_sdk.runtime.peripherals.providers.ble import bluez as bluez_pairing

    assert bluez_pairing.device_path("hci0", "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff") == DEVICE
    assert bluez_pairing.agent_answer(member, body, DEVICE) == answer
